ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Bayyina means an innate conviction and belief from God that guides a person, provided bad company has not distorted his nature.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It refers to the conviction and belief innately found in a person from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The goodly provision granted to Shu’ayb is revelation, parallel to the way material sustenance supports the body and revelation sustains the spirit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: divine revelation is need for sustaining his spiritual being.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Jesus
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus is reported as saying that people need God’s word as well as physical bread.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Jesus (sws) is reported to have said: “Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The conditional clause’s answer is omitted and supplied from 11:63: if Shu’ayb has clear evidence and revelation, deviation would leave him without rescue from divine wrath.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The answer to the conditional clause in the first part of the verse is suppressed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Shu’ayb’s call arose from his heart even before revelation, and revelation later substantiated it; the mockery falsely treats his earnest preaching as contrived.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: what he has said to them was the call of his heart even before he received divine revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Shu’ayb denies that he is stopping dishonest trade to monopolize the market; opponents may have spread that allegation because he had a small business.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: his purpose was to make them honest while he himself takes control of the market

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: He wants only to reform matters as far as possible and relies on God’s grace, trust, and turning to Him for help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he only wants to mend affairs as far as he could.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the answer to ‘Have you considered?’ is omitted: if Shuʿayb truly has clear proof and prophethood, he must command them to abandon idols and sins, as that is why prophets are sent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r1.anchor: ومعنى الكلام يناوي عليه، والمعنى أخبروني إن كنت على حجة واضحة ويقين من ربي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says calling the proposed clause the answer to ‘Have you considered?’ is not technical: it is the second object of the verb when it means ‘inform me.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r2.anchor: وتسمية هذا جوابا لأرأيتم ليس بالمصطلح، بل هذه الجملة التي قدرها هي في موضع المفعول الثاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r3.claim: Al-Hawfi says the conditional answer is omitted and estimates: would I turn away from my worship on this basis?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي: وجواب الشرط محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya estimates the omitted conditional answer as ‘would I go astray as you have,’ or abandon delivering the message, or a similar response fitting the argument.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وجواب الشرط الذي في قوله: إن كنت على بينة من ربي محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects ‘I would go astray’ as the conditional answer: if declarative, it does not follow from the condition; if interrogative with an omitted hamza, it is the second object of ‘Have you considered?’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r5.anchor: وليس قوله: أضل جوابا للشرط، لأنه إن كان مثبتا فلا يمكن أن يكون جوابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r6.claim: ‘Good provision’ apparently means lawful, wholesome wealth acquired without short measure or fraud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r6.anchor: والظاهر في قوله: رزقا حسنا أنه الحلال الطيب من غير بخس ولا تطفيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses ‘good provision’ as lawful wealth; Shuʿayb had abundant wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحلال، وكان شعيب عليه السلام كثير المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r8.claim: Other interpretations of ‘good provision’ are prophethood or knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r8.anchor: وكان شعيب عليه السلام كثير المال. وقيل: النبوة. وقيل: العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya explains that Shuʿayb does not intend to do the short-measuring and weight-cheating he forbids, then monopolize the money.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r9.anchor: من نقص الكيل والوزن وأستأثر بالمال قاله: ابن عطية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r10.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r10.claim: Qatada says Shuʿayb would not forbid an action and then commit it himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: لم أكن لأنهاكم عن أمر ثم أرتكبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r11.speaker: صاحب الغنيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r11.claim: The author of al-Ghunyān understands the phrase as refusing to do privately what Shuʿayb forbids publicly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r11.anchor: وقال صاحب الغنيان: ما أريد أن أخالفكم في السر إلى ما أنهاكم عنه في العلانية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r12.claim: In usage, ‘he opposed me toward it’ means he headed toward something while I turned away; ‘he opposed me away from it’ means the reverse, illustrated by travelers meeting at water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p198/r12.anchor: ويقال: خالفني فلان إلى كذا إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه، وخالفني عنه إذا ولى عنه وأنت قاصده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r1.claim: The sense is that Shuʿayb would get ahead of them in the desires he forbids and reserve them for himself; grammatically, ‘that I oppose you’ may be the object of ‘I want,’ with khālafa meaning ‘followed behind.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r1.anchor: والمعنى أن أسبقكم إلى شهواتكم التي نهيتكم عنها لأستبد بها دونكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r2.claim: One analysis makes ‘toward’ attach to ‘oppose,’ or to an omitted phrase meaning ‘inclined toward what I forbid.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r2.anchor: وتتعلق إلى بأخالفكم، أو بمحذوف أي: مائلا إلى ما أنهاكم عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r3.claim: Another analysis retains the apparent sense of opposition and supplies ‘inclined toward’; alternatively, the clause is a purpose complement, with ‘toward’ attached to ‘I want.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r3.anchor: أو يبقى أن أخالفكم على ظاهر ما يفهم من المخالفة، ويكون في موضع المفعول به بأريد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads the phrase as ‘I do not intend, by opposing you, to undertake what I forbid you.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال الزجاج: وما أقصد بخلافكم إلى ارتكاب ما أنهاكم عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r5.claim: ‘As long as I can’ is apparently a time clause: for as long as Shuʿayb can reform, he will spare no effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن ما مصدرية ظرفية أي مدة استطاعتي للإصلاح، وما دمت متمكنا منه لا آلوا فيه جهدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers two analyses of ‘except reform as much as I can’: it may replace ‘reform,’ or include an omitted noun, ‘reform of what I can.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r6.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري في ما وجوها أحدها: أن يكون بدلا من الإصلاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's third analysis makes the phrase an object, as in a poetic example: Shuʿayb seeks only to repair as much of their corruption as he can.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r7.anchor: والثالث: أن يكون مفعولا كقوله: ضعيف النكاية أعداءه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan calls that third analysis weak: Kufans disallow a definite verbal noun with al- from governing a direct object, and Basrans allow it only rarely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r8.anchor: وهذا الثالث ضعيف، لأن المصدر المعرف بأل لا يجوز إعماله في المفعول به عند الكوفيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r9.claim: ‘My success’ means either divine aid for calling them to worship God alone and avoid what He forbids, or aid in keeping one's actions rightly aligned with God's pleasure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r9.anchor: وما توفيقي أي لدعائكم إلى عبادة الله وحده، وترك ما نهاكم عنه إلا بمعونة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r10.claim: His reliance is on God alone and to Him he returns in all speech and action; this asks for divine support, threatens disbelievers, and removes their hope of harming him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p199/r10.anchor: وفي هذا طلب التأييد من الله تعالى، وتهديد للكفار وحسم لأطماعهم أن ينالوه بشر

THALABI:v5p186/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r7.claim: Shuayb says he has clear proof from God and lawful, wholesome provision, without cheating or shortchanging.
THALABI:v5p186/r7.anchor: قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة حجة وبصيرة وبيان وبرهان من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا حلالا طيبا من غير بخس ولا تطفيف

THALABI:v5p186/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r8.claim: An alternate gloss understands the good provision as knowledge and understanding.
THALABI:v5p186/r8.anchor: طيبا من غير بخس ولا تطفيف، وقيل: علما ومعرفة

THALABI:v5p186/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r9.claim: Shuayb says he does not intend to do what he forbids others to do.
THALABI:v5p186/r9.anchor: وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه ما أريد أن أنهاكم عن أمر وأرتكبه

THALABI:v5p186/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r10.claim: Shuayb seeks reform as far as he can; his success depends only on God, on whom he relies.
THALABI:v5p186/r10.anchor: إن أريد ما أريد فيما آمركم به وأنهاكم عنه إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي إلا بالله عليه توكلت

THALABI:v5p186/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p186/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p186/r11.claim: The author says anib means returning to God amid calamities, or returning to Him in the Hereafter.
THALABI:v5p186/r11.anchor: وإليه أنيب أي أرجع فيما ينزل بي من النوائب

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r1.claim: Words divide into nouns, verbs, and particles by whether they can be reported of and used to report: nouns do both, verbs only the latter, particles neither.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r1.anchor: أن الكلمة إما أن يصح الإخبار عنها وبها وهي الاسم وإما أن لا يصح الإخبار عنها لكن يصح الإخبار بها

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r2.speaker: النحويون
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r2.claim: Grammarians agree that verbs and particles cannot be subjects of predication; Razi says the lone examples offered do not establish a general rule.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r2.anchor: اتفق النحويون على أن الفعل والحرف لا يصح الإخبار عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r3.claim: Calling the forms ضرب يضرب أضرب verbs predicates of them; treating the referents as nouns returns to the initial disputed distinction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r3.anchor: أنا إذا أخبرنا عن ضرب يضرب أضرب بأنها أفعال فالمخبر عنه في هذا الخبر

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r4.claim: Saying that a verb and particle are not nouns itself predicates something of them, challenging the claim that they cannot be reported on.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r4.anchor: إذا أخبرنا عن الفعل والحرف بأنه ليس باسم فالتقدير عين ما تقدم

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r5.claim: The statement that verbs cannot be reported on is itself a report about a verb; treating its referent as a mere word-form repeats the earlier problem.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r5.anchor: المخبر عنه بأنه لا يخبر عنه إن كان اسما فهو باطل

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r6.claim: A verb as verb and a particle as particle are distinct known essences, so one can report that each is distinguished from other things.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r6.anchor: الفعل من حيث هو فعل والحرف من حيث هو حرف ماهية معلومة متميزة عما عداها

RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r7.claim: Whether a verb means its form, which signifies a meaning, or the meaning signified, it can be reported on as signifier or signified.
RAZI-FULL:v1p37#2/r7.anchor: الفعل إما أن يكون عبارة عن الصيغة الدالة على المعنى المخصوص وإما أن يكون عبارة عن ذلك المعنى المخصوص

STUDYQURAN:11:88/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r1.claim: Shuʿayb’s clear proof is said to consist of miracles God grants prophets to prove their veracity.
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r1.anchor: which are given to all prophets by God to prove their veracity; see 7:85c.

STUDYQURAN:11:88/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r2.claim: The familiar expression says that success and its blessing in this world and the next ultimately depend on God.
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r2.anchor: it conveys the idea that no matter what one does, it is ultimately up to God whether it will be successful and carry a blessing in this world and in the next.

STUDYQURAN:11:88/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r3.claim: Shuʿayb’s reliance and turning to God echoes the statement taught to the Prophet and links to the earlier Shuʿayb passage.
STUDYQURAN:11:88/r3.anchor: Shuʿayb’s statement In Him do I trust and unto Him do I turn is identical to the statement the Prophet is taught to make in 42:10; see also 7:88–89c.

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r1.claim: Shuaib asks them to consider whether he has proof from his Lord in calling them to worship Allah alone and reject idols, and in forbidding financial corruption.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r1.anchor: فيما أدعوكم إليه من عبادة الله، والبراءة من عبادة الأوثان والأصنام

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r2.claim: The good provision Allah gave Shuaib means lawful, wholesome provision.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r2.anchor: {ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا} [هود: 88] يعني حلالا طيبا.

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r3.claim: He does not forbid a practice and then do it himself; he acts by what he commands and refrains from what he forbids.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r3.anchor: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} [هود: 88] يقول: وما أريد أن أنهاكم عن أمر ثم أفعل خلافه

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r4.claim: Qatada says Shuaib would not forbid them from doing something that he himself practiced.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} [هود: 88] يقول: لم أكن لأنهاكم عن أمر أركبه

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r5.claim: Shuaib seeks only to reform them and their affairs as far as he can, so they avoid God's exemplary punishment for disobeying Him and His messenger.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r5.anchor: ما أريد فيما آمركم به، وأنهاكم عنه، إلا إصلاحكم وإصلاح أمركم

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r6.claim: His ability to reach the truth while seeking their reform depends entirely on Allah's aid; without it he would not attain the right.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r6.anchor: وما إصابتي الحق في محاولتي إصلاحكم وإصلاح أمركم إلا بالله، فإنه هو المعين على ذلك

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r7.claim: Shuaib entrusts his affairs to Allah, on whom he relies and in whom he has confidence.
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r7.anchor: إلى الله أفوض أمري، فإنه ثقتي وعليه اعتمادي في أموري

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r8.claim: To Allah he turns through obedience and returns in repentance.

TAB-FULL:v12p549/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p549/r9.claim: Mujahid glosses أنيب as I return.

TAB-FULL:v12p550/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p550/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p550/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses أنيب as I return.
TAB-FULL:v12p550/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله: " {وإليه أنيب} [هود: 88] قال: أرجع "

TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.claim: They attribute the command to prayer because it urges Shuʿayb to oppose their idol worship and short measure; he answers by describing his instruction as a prohibition.
TABATABAI:11:86-88/r6.anchor: لما فيها من البعث والدعوة إلى معارضة القوم في عبادتهم الأصنام ونقصهم المكيال والميزان

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r6.claim: Being upon a clear proof means possessing the sign of prophethood, a miracle demonstrating the prophet’s truth.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r6.anchor: وهي آية النبوة والمعجزة الدالة على صدق النبي

TABATABAI:11:87-88/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r7.claim: The good provision God gave Shuʿayb is prophetic revelation containing foundational knowledge and religious laws.
TABATABAI:11:87-88/r7.anchor: والمراد بكونه رزق من الله رزقا حسنا أن الله آتاه من لدنه وحي النبوة المشتمل على أصول المعارف والشرائع

TABATABAI:11:88/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r1.claim: Shuʿayb asks whether a messenger supported by proof and revelation is foolish or tyrannical: God owns all, and people are not free to refuse His commands.
TABATABAI:11:88/r1.anchor: فهل أنا سفيه في رأيي؟ وهل ما أدعوكم إليه دعوة سفهية؟ وهل في ذلك تحكم مني عليكم أو سلب مني لحريتكم؟

TABATABAI:11:88/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r2.claim: The preposition ilā follows khālafa because the verb is understood to include the sense of inclination: either opposing them while inclining toward the forbidden act, or inclining toward it in opposition to them.
TABATABAI:11:88/r2.anchor: تعدية المخالفة بإلى لتضمينه معنى ما يتعدى بها كالميل ونحوه

TABATABAI:11:88/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r3.claim: His denial answers their charge that he seeks to strip their freedom, enslave them, and control them; he does not practice what he forbids, so his aim is reform.
TABATABAI:11:88/r3.anchor: والجملة جواب عن ما اتهموه به أنه يريد أن يسلب عنهم الحرية في أعمالهم ويستعبدهم ويتحكم عليهم

TABATABAI:11:88/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r4.claim: Humans are innately free in action and equal relative to their fellow humans, so no one may arbitrarily dominate another.
TABATABAI:11:88/r4.anchor: فله بحسب هذه النشأة حرية تامة بالقياس إلى بني نوعه الذين هم أمثاله وأشباهه في الخلقة لهم ما له وعليهم ما عليه

TABATABAI:11:88/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r5.claim: Human life depends on society, cooperation, rules, and government to preserve order and serve shared interests.
TABATABAI:11:88/r5.anchor: ومن البديهي أن الاجتماع لا يقوم على ساق إلا بسنن وقوانين تجري فيها، وحكومة يتولاها بعضهم تحفظ النظم وتجري القوانين

TABATABAI:11:88/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88/r6.claim: People surrender some freedom under common law to secure shared wellbeing; limiting conduct that harms vital interests is not enslavement, and an admonisher voices the society’s collective needs.
TABATABAI:11:88/r6.anchor: وإنما الواحد الذي يلقي إليهم الأمر والنهي بمنزلة لسان ناطق لا يزيد على ذلك

TABATABAI:11:88#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r1.claim: A person naturally protects his interests, so if Shuʿayb saw good in the work he recommends to others, he would not contradict it in his own conduct.
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r1.anchor: إذ الإنسان مطبوع على التحفظ على منافعه ورعاية مصالحه فلو كان فيما يدعو إليه غيره من العمل خير وهو مشترك بينهما لم يخالفه بشخصه

TABATABAI:11:88#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r2.claim: Shuʿayb’s refusal to seek payment, as stated in 26:109, further rebuts suspicion that he preaches for private advantage.
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r2.anchor: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

TABATABAI:11:88#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r3.claim: What Shuʿayb forbids benefits the society to which he belongs and is an obligation for all its members, not a self-serving demand.
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r3.anchor: إلى أن الذي ينهاهم عنه من الأمور التي فيها صلاح مجتمعهم الذي هو أحد أفراده، ويجب على الجميع مراعاتها وملازمتها

TABATABAI:11:88#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r4.claim: His stated purpose is only to reform the community to the extent he can.
TABATABAI:11:88#2/r4.anchor: عقبه بقوله { إن أريد إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت }

TABATABAI:11:88#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r1.claim: Shuʿayb acknowledges that his success comes from God, a consequence of God’s creation and sustaining of every soul.
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r1.anchor: بين عليه السلام هذه الحقيقة، واعترف بأن توفيقه بالله، وذلك من فروع كونه تعالى

TABATABAI:11:88#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r2.claim: God originates and preserves every soul and its deeds, as affirmed in 35:1, 34:21, 13:33, and 35:41.
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r2.anchor: وذلك من فروع كونه تعالى هو الفاطر لكل نفس والحافظ عليها والقائم على كل نفس بما كسبت

TABATABAI:11:88#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r3.claim: All things, actions, and relations are attributable to God, who encompasses and governs them, while each thing also has its relation to them by His permission.
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r3.anchor: ولها مع ذلك نسبة إلى ذلك الشيء بإذنه تعالى

TABATABAI:11:88#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r4.claim: A servant who understands God’s sustaining role should embody it by entrusting himself to God and returning to Him.
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r4.anchor: ومن الواجب للعبد العالم بمقام ربه العارف بهذه الحقيقة أن يمثلها بإنشاء التوكل على ربه والإنابة والرجوع إليه

TABATABAI:11:88#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r5.claim: A person is compelled to possess the capacity for choice but remains free to choose each action or its omission; this is innate human freedom.
TABATABAI:11:88#3/r5.anchor: فهو مضطر في التلبس والاتصاف بأصل الاختيار لكنه مختار في الأفعال المنتسبة إليه الصادرة عنه باختياره

TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r1.claim: In al-Maʿānī, Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq explains that obedience accords with God’s command; if God blocks an intended sin and the servant leaves it, that too is divine success, whereas allowing the sin is abandonment. The report also asks about 3:160.
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت فقوله عز وجل { وما توفيقي إلا بالله }

TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r2.claim: The author explains divine success and abandonment as active attributes: God arranges causes toward good or withholds causes that facilitate sin; the servant is described by the resulting relation.
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r2.anchor: أقول محصل بيانه عليه السلام أن توفيقه تعالى وخذلانه من صفاته الفعلية

TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r3.claim: Ali asks the Prophet for advice; the Prophet says to affirm God as Lord and remain upright. Ali answers with the verse’s trust and success language, and the Prophet praises his deep knowledge.
TABATABAI:11:84-95#3/r3.anchor: عن علي قال قلت يا رسول الله أوصني. قال قل ربي الله ثم استقم

TABRISI:11:87/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:87/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:87/r10.claim: Tawfīq means correctness, especially correctness that occurs in obedience; only God can guide to it because He alone knows its conditions without instruction.
TABRISI:11:87/r10.anchor: والتوفيق من الصواب إلا أنه اختص بهذا الاسم ما اتفق وقوع الصواب عنده

TABRISI:11:84-95/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:11:84-95/r12.claim: One gloss identifies Shuʿayb's good provision as prophethood.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r12.anchor: قيل: إن الرزق الحسن ههنا النبوة

TABRISI:11:84-95/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:11:84-95/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means God guided him to His religion and expanded his wealth, for he was wealthy.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r13.anchor: وقيل: معناه هداني لدينه ووسع علي رزقه وكان كثير المال عن الحسن

TABRISI:11:84-95/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r14.claim: Another view takes every blessing from God as good provision.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r14.anchor: وقيل: كل نعمة من الله سبحانه فهو رزق حسن

TABRISI:11:84-95/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r15.claim: The omitted continuation asks whether, after this favor, Shuʿayb would abandon worship; the retained words indicate the ellipsis.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r15.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف أي أفأعدل مع ذلك عما أنا عليه من عبادته

TABRISI:11:84-95/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95/r16.claim: Shuʿayb does not forbid something and then practice it himself; he chooses for them what he chooses for himself.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r16.anchor: أي لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه وإنما أختار لكم ما أختاره لنفسي

TABRISI:11:84-95/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95/r17.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:11:84-95/r17.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the construction as Shuʿayb intending to do the forbidden act in opposition to them.
TABRISI:11:84-95/r17.anchor: ما أخالفكم إليه ما أقصده بخلافكم إلى ارتكابه عن الزجاج

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r1.claim: The cited poem condemns someone who forbids a trait and then does it himself, supporting Shuʿayb's claim of consistency.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r1.anchor: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r2.claim: Another view says he does not seek to draw personal gain from what he forbids, such as keeping the profit from short measure.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه وما أريد اجترار منفعة إلى نفسي بما أنهاكم عنه

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r3.claim: His commands and prohibitions aim only to set right the people's religious and worldly affairs.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r3.anchor: لست أريد بما آمركم به وأنهاكم عنه إلا اصلاح أموركم في دينكم ودنياكم

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r4.claim: The phrase means as much as he is able and capable.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r4.anchor: أي ما قدرت عليه وتمكنت منه

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r5.claim: His ability to obey and refrain comes only from God; it is not his own power but God's assistance, grace, and facilitation.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r5.anchor: وليس ما أفعله بحولي وقوتي بل بمعونة الله ولطفه وتيسيره

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r6.claim: Tawakkul is contentment with God's governance, entrusting matters to Him, and holding fast to obedience.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r6.anchor: والتوكل على الله الرضا بتدبيره مع تفويض الأمور إليه والتمسك بطاعته

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid interprets Shuʿayb's return as his return to God at the resurrection.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r7.anchor: أي وإليه أرجع في المعاد عن مجاهد

TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says he returns to God through his deeds and intention, directing all his works to God.
TABRISI:11:84-95#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: إليه أرجع بعملي ونيتي عن الحسن ومعناه أني أعمل أعمالي كلها لوجه الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r1.claim: The explanation of this conditional expression was given earlier in two places in the surah, at 11:28 and 11:63.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r1.anchor: مضى هذا في موضعين من هذه السورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and most commentators say the good provision is lawful provision.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين (¬3): يعني حلالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi reports that Shuayb possessed great wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r3.anchor: وروى الكلبي (¬4): أن شعيبا كان كثير المال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Shuayb counts abundant wealth as God's blessing because it was lawful and free of liabilities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: اعتد بكثرة المال نعمة من الله تعالى لما كان حلالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r5.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r5.claim: Another group of commentators takes good provision to mean guidance and success in right conduct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r5.anchor: وقال جماعة من المفسرين: الرزق الحسن هاهنا: الهدى والتوفيق للرشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r6.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer: if God gave me proof and lawful wealth, would I follow error and cheat? The point is that lawful wealth made him independent of cheating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬5) وغيره: جواب (إن) هاهنا محذوف لعلم المخاطب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses this as: I do not intend to do what I forbid you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): يريد وما أريد أن أفعل ما أنهاكم عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r8.claim: Qatada says Shuayb does not forbid a thing and then commit it himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة (¬3): لم أكن لأنهاكم عن أمر ثم أرتكبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq explains that Shuayb neither forbids something and then enters into it himself nor chooses for them what he rejects for himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r9.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬5): أي لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r10.claim: To oppose them toward something means to set out to do that thing contrary to them; Shuayb is not doing what he forbids.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r10.anchor: وتلخيص معنى اللفظ: وما أخالفكم بالقصد إلى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r11.claim: Shuayb's call to obey God and abandon cheating is the course he chooses for himself, showing sincere counsel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p527/r11.anchor: وقال أبو بكر: بين أن الذي يدعوهم إليه من اتباع طاعة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r1.claim: Shuayb seeks only to repair relations by having them worship God alone and act as God-fearing people do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r1.anchor: أي ما أريد إلا الإصلاح فيما بيني وبينكم بأن تعبدوا الله وحده وتفعلوا كما يفعل من يخاف الله، قاله ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r2.claim: The object of what he can do is omitted: he means as much reform as he can accomplish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r2.anchor: مفعول الاستطاعة محذوف تقديره ما استطعته، أي ما استطعت الإصلاح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r3.claim: His capacity for reform is limited to conveying the message and warning; he cannot force them to obey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى قول أبي إسحاق (¬1)؛ لأنه قال في قوله {ما استطعت}: أي بقدر طاقتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r4.claim: Neither Shuayb nor anyone else can obey except through God's enabling and success.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r4.anchor: لا يقدر هو ولا غيره على الطاعة إلا بتوفيق الله جل وعز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say Shuayb returns to God at the resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r5.anchor: أي أرجع إليه في المعاد في قول ابن عباس (¬3) ومجاهد (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says he returns to God through his deeds and intention.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬5): إليه أرجع بعملي ونيتي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r7.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r7.claim: The Prophet called Shuayb the orator of the prophets because of his skill in addressing and responding to his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p528/r7.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا ذكر شعيبا قال: "ذاك خطيب الأنبياء"

QASHANI:11:88/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:88/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:88/r3.claim: Shuayb asks whether, given certain proof of unity and a good gift from God—wisdom, perfection, and the ability to perfect others—he could abandon his mission.
QASHANI:11:88/r3.anchor: من الحكمة العلمية والعملية والكمال والتكميل بالاستقامة في التوحيد، هل يصح لي أن أترك

QASHANI:11:88/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:88/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:88/r4.claim: He does not seek transient worldly profit by committing the injustice he forbids.
QASHANI:11:88/r4.anchor: أي: أن أقصد إلى أجر المنافع الدنيوية الفانية بارتكاب الظلم الذي أنهاكم عنه

QASHANI:11:88/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:88/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:88/r5.claim: His only aim is to reform himself and his people through purification and preparation to receive wisdom, as far as he can.
QASHANI:11:88/r5.anchor: إصلاح نفسي ونفوسكم بالتزكية والتهيئة لقبول الحكمة ما دمت مستطيعا

QASHANI:11:88/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:88/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:88/r6.claim: His ability to reform comes only from God; he trusts in God and turns back to Him.
QASHANI:11:88/r6.anchor: إلا بالله عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r1.anchor: قال يا قوم أرأيتم } أعلمتم { إن كنت على بينة من ربي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r2.claim: The proof from his Lord is clear evidence and an argument.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r3.claim: The good provision is lawful wealth; Shuayb had a great deal of money.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r3.anchor: حلالا، وذلك أنه كان كثير المال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r4.claim: The answer to 'if' is omitted: would he, with proof and lawful wealth, follow error by cheating and short-measuring?
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r4.anchor: على معنى: إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني المال الحلال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r5.claim: He does not forbid them from something and then do it himself; he chooses for them what he chooses for himself.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r5.anchor: لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه، وإنما أختار لكم ما أختار لنفسي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r6.claim: He seeks to set right his relationship with them by calling them to worship God alone and act as God-fearing people do.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r6.anchor: ما أريد { إلا الإصلاح } فيما بيني وبينكم بأن تعبدوا الله وحده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r7.claim: This means as far as his ability to convey the message and warn permits.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r7.anchor: أي: بقدر طاقتي، وطاقة الإبلاغ والإنذار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r8.claim: Neither Shuayb nor anyone else can obey except through God's enabling grace.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r8.anchor: لا يقدر هو ولا غيره على الطاعة إلا بتوفيق الله سبحانه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:88/r9.claim: He returns to God at the Resurrection.

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r1.claim: “Have you considered?” means “Have you seen your condition? If so, tell me what you say.”
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r1.anchor: gördünüz mü hâlinizi yani gördünüzse söyleyin bakayım

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r2.claim: Shuaib's clear proof from his Lord is decisive evidence; if he speaks through knowledge and prophethood, how could he oppose his Lord's revelation and explanation?
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r2.anchor: Rabbim Hak teâlâ’dan kat‘î ve açık bir burhan üzerinde bulunuyor, söylediklerimi ilm ü nübüvvetle söylüyorsam ne dersiniz? Ben Rabbimin vahy ü beyânına muhalefet edebilir miyim?

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r3.claim: The good provision is bestowed from God's treasury, not earned by Shuaib himself; it includes lawful material wealth and the spiritual gifts of prophethood and wisdom, means of eternal life.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r3.anchor: hazîne-i kereminden beni maddeten mânen güzel bir surette merzuk etmiş, hem helâlinden mal hem de ebedî hayatın medârı olan nübüvvet ve hikmet nasip eylemiştir

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r4.claim: Shuaib does not forbid them shirk, violating people's rights, and corruption in order to do those things himself; his advice to adopt monotheism and justice is not a scheme to seize their freedom and reserve the forbidden conduct for himself.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r4.anchor: murâdım, gāye-i maksadım hürriyetinizi alıp sizi çevirip de o menhiyyâtı münhasıran kendim yapmak değildir

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r5.claim: He is not plotting tyranny or monopoly so that they avoid sin, cheating, and consuming people's property while he does those things and claims pleasure for himself.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r5.anchor: Allah’a karşı siz günaha girmeyin de ben gireyim, siz aldatmayın da ben aldatayım, halkın emvâlini siz yemeyin de ben yiyeyim

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r6.claim: His sole aim is to bring about reform as far as he is able.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r6.anchor: Muradım başka değil, gücüm yettikçe ıslahtan ibarettir

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r7.claim: His success comes only through God's guidance and grace.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r7.anchor: Muvaffakiyetim de ancak Allah iledir. Allah’ın hidâyet ve inâyetiyledir

ELMALILI:11:88-90/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r9.claim: To turn in repentance means repeatedly returning to God, seeking His protection, and submitting to Him.
ELMALILI:11:88-90/r9.anchor: döner döner O’na dönerim, O’na dehâlet eder, O’na teslim olurum

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r1.claim: Similar statements by Muhammad and other prophets appeared earlier in verses 17, 28, and 63 of this surah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r1.anchor: Buna benzer âyetler (17, 28, 63) daha önce Hz. Muhammed ve diğer peygamberlerle ilgili olarak geçmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r2.claim: Like the other prophets, Shuaib said he had rational and revealed evidence for the monotheistic faith and moral principles he preached, and asked his people to consider it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r2.anchor: tevhid inancı ve ahlâk ilkeleri konusunda kendisinin aklî ve naklî delillere sahip olduğunu açıkladı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r3.claim: The good provision God gave Shuaib may mean lawful wealth for material needs, prophethood as a spiritual station, or both.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r3.anchor: Allah tarafından kendisine verilen güzel rızıktan maksat maddî ihtiyaçlarını karşılayacağı helâl mal olabileceği gibi yüce ve mânevî bir makam olan peygamberlik görevi de olabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r4.claim: After using his material and spiritual means to preach with full effort, Shuaib stresses that success also depends on God's will and that he relies on God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r4.anchor: maddî ve mânevî imkânlarını kullanarak bütün gücüyle onu tebliğ etmeye çalıştıktan sonra, başarının Allah’ın iradesinin de aynı yönde tecelli etmesine bağlı olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r5.claim: Trust in God is not an excuse for passivity; it is sincere reliance, sustained hope, and effort through difficulty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r5.anchor: Allah’a dayanıp güvenme yani “tevekkül” uyuşukluk ve hareketsizliğin bir mazereti değil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r6.claim: Shuaib's words summarize a mature guide's qualities: reliance on revealed proof, personal consistency, sound reform efforts, trust in God as the source of success, and perseverance without despair.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:88/r6.anchor: mürşid-i kâmilde bulunması gereken vasıfları da özetlemiş bulunmaktadır

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r2.claim: Shuayb’s listeners answered his counsel with stubborn persistence in denial and ingratitude, relying on ignorance and imitation rather than reflection or insight into guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r2.anchor: لم يقابلوا نصيحته لهم إلا بالعناد والتمادي فيما هو دائم من الجحد والكنود

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r3.claim: A clear proof is a light that lets one perceive what is hidden beneath the covering of heedlessness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r3.anchor: البينة نور تستبصر به ما خفي عليك تحت غطاء الغفلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r4.claim: Good provision sustains independence and comes from God’s primordial care and good governance of a person’s welfare, completing blessing and preserving protection.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r4.anchor: والرزق الحسن ما به دوام الاستقلال ، وما ذلك إلا مقتضى عنايته الأزلية

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r5.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r5.claim: One reported view defines good provision as what a person strives to obtain but receives without fatigue.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r5.anchor: وقيل الرزق الحسن ما تعني صاحبه لطلبه ، ولم يصبه نصب بسببه

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r6.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r6.claim: Another reported view defines good provision as what one receives while witnessing it as provision and retaining awareness of the Provider while enjoying it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r6.anchor: وقيل الرزق الحسن ما يستوفيه بشهود الرزق ويحفظه عند التنعم بوجود الرزاق

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r7.claim: A further saying defines good provision as what does not make its recipient forget the Provider and instead moves the recipient to generosity and spending.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r7.anchor: ويقال الرزق الحسن ما لا ينسي الرزاق ، ويحمل صاحبه على التوسعة والإنفاق

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r8.claim: A preacher may be lenient about what he commands, since performing every duty is impossible, but must not permit what he forbids, since avoiding all prohibitions is obligatory.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r8.anchor: فإن الإتيان بجميع الطاعات غير ممكن ، ولكن التجرد عن جميع المحرمات واجب

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r9.claim: A person who cannot restrain their own soul from desire has no authority to guide others toward right guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r9.anchor: من لم يكن له حكم على نفسه في المنع عن الهوى لم يكن له حكم على غيره

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r10.claim: Good intention to reform what one can is central to action, and God joins it with facilitation; when someone intends evil, God leaves that person to obstruction.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r10.anchor: مدار الأمر إلى الأغراض المقضية حسن القصد بالإصلاح ، فيقرن الله به حسن التيسير

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r11.claim: In religious usage, enabling success is the capacity by which obedience is performed; more broadly, divinely supplied motives and means of obedience count as enabling success.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r11.anchor: وفي الشريعة التوفيق ما تنفق به الطاعة ، وهو قدرة الطاعة ، ثم كل ما تقرب العبد به من الطاعة

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r12.claim: Enabling success comes through and from God, who bestows it as a gracious favor.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r12.anchor: والتوفيق بالله ومن الله ، وهو - سبحانه - بإعطائه متفضل

QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r13.claim: Reliance delegates one’s affairs to God; its sign is leaving personal planning through witness of the decree and trusting the promise when its fulfillment is not yet present.
QUSHAYRI:v2p54/r13.anchor: التوكل تفويض الأمر إلى الله ، وأمارته ترك التدبير بشهود التقدير

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r1.claim: Poets reuse the image of a ruler’s power reaching everywhere: al-Farazdaq fails to match al-Nābigha’s wording and meaning, while al-Akhṭal and later poets adapt it.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r1.anchor: فلم يأت بالمعنى ولا اللفظ على ما سبق إليه النابغة

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r2.speaker: النبي
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r2.claim: The Prophet’s saying that he was aided by terror and that the religion would reach wherever night reaches offers a related image.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r2.anchor: وقد روى نحو هذا عن النبي نصرت بالرعب وجعل رزقي تحت ظل رمحي وليدخلن هذا الدين على ما دخل عليه الليل

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r3.claim: The same image is successively reworked by ʿAlī ibn Jabala, Sallām al-Khāsir, and al-Buḥturī, whose verse imagines fugitives escaping even to the stars.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r3.anchor: ولو أنهم ركبوا الكواكب لم يكن ينجيهم عن خوف بأسك مهرب

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r4.claim: He illustrates poetic metaphor with examples from Zuhayr, al-Aʿshā, Nuṣayb, and Taʾabbaṭa Sharran.

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r9.claim: Poetic hyperbole is illustrated by al-Namir ibn Tawlab, al-Nābigha, and ʿAntara, whose images exaggerate a sword’s force, armor, and a warrior’s response.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r9.anchor: ومن البديع عندهم الغلو والإفراط في الصفة كقول النمر بن تولب

BURHAN:v4p152/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r1.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v4p152/r1.claim: Treating the address marker in أرأيتم as a pronoun is defensible: mental-seeing verbs may take a connected pronoun as their object in the cited constructions.
BURHAN:v4p152/r1.anchor: من جعل الاداة المؤكد بها الخطاب في ارايتكم ضمير لم يلزمه اعتراض

BURHAN:v4p152/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r2.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v4p152/r2.claim: The majority analyze the emphatic address element in أرأيتم as a particle, which removes the syntactic objection.
BURHAN:v4p152/r2.anchor: وأما من جرد اداة الخطاب المؤكد بها للحرفية وهو قول الجمهور فلا كلام في ذلك

BURHAN:v4p152/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r3.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p152/r3.claim: Sibawayh says the kāf in أرأيتم has no syntactic case.

BURHAN:v4p152/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r4.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v4p152/r4.claim: Al-Sakkaki assigns the kāf in أرأيتم the accusative case.

BURHAN:v4p152/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r5.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v4p152/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ assigns the kāf in أرأيتم the nominative case.

BURHAN:v4p152/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p152/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p152/r8.claim: In its second use, أرأيتم means pay attention and need not be interrogative; the expected answer is omitted here as understood.
BURHAN:v4p152/r8.anchor: والثاني تكون فيه بمعنى انتبه كقولك ارايت زيدا فاني احبه أي انتبه له

SULAMI:v1p324/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p324/r1.claim: A preacher who speaks without acting is no true preacher; wisdom requires wise speech, action, and conduct in every state.
SULAMI:v1p324/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : ليس بواعظ من كان واعظا بلسانه دون عمله ،

SULAMI:v1p324/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r2.claim: God told Jesus to admonish himself first: if he does not heed the admonition, he should be ashamed before God.
SULAMI:v1p324/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن الله عز وجل أوحى إلى عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم يا عيسى عظ نفسك ، فإن اتعظت ،

SULAMI:v1p324/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r3.claim: The speaker seeks the people's rectification if God grants success, and cannot accomplish it without God's help.
SULAMI:v1p324/r3.anchor: قيل فيه : مرادي صلاحكم إن ساعدكم التوفيق ، ولا أستطيع أنا ذلك لكم إلا بمعونة

SULAMI:v1p324/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r4.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v1p324/r4.claim: Divine success is gracious care directed to a servant without a cause or merit that the servant can claim.
SULAMI:v1p324/r4.anchor: قال النهرجوري : التوفيق حسن عناية سيق إلى العبد ليس فيه سبب ولا منة إليه طلب .

SULAMI:v1p324/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r5.claim: Success is a guide to truth and away from falsehood, bringing the servant the care decreed for him eternally.
SULAMI:v1p324/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : التوفيق هو الدليل الذي يدل على سبيل الحق ، ويبعد عن نهج الباطل ،

SULAMI:v1p324/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r6.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p324/r6.claim: Reliance means showing no agitation toward causes despite severe need and not abandoning true gratitude to God while using them.
SULAMI:v1p324/r6.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : التوكل أن لا يظهر فيك انزعاج إلى الأسباب مع شدة الفاقة ،

SULAMI:v1p324/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r7.claim: Reliance is ceasing to regard one's own reliance, dropping the intermediaries from view, and clinging to the strongest bond.
SULAMI:v1p324/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : التوكل : ترك رؤية التوكل وإسقاط رؤية الوسائط ، والتعلق بأعلى الوثائق .

SULAMI:v1p324/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r8.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r8.claim: Reliance makes resting on predators' thighs and reclining on cushions equally acceptable.
SULAMI:v1p324/r8.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن أدهم رحمه الله : التوكل : أن تستوي عندك أفخاذ السباع ، والمتكأ على الجشايا .

SULAMI:v1p324/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p324/r9.claim: Returning to God means turning back from all one has and owes and relying on no one besides Him.
SULAMI:v1p324/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ' وإليه أنيب ' : قال إليه أرجع عن جميع ما لي وعلي ،

SULAMI:v1p324/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p324/r10.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p324/r10.claim: Inaba begins by turning from all one's own claims; when perfected, the return is from God to God, dissolving the separate returner in witnessing Him.
SULAMI:v1p324/r10.anchor: قال بعضهم : الإنابة : هي الرجوع عن جميع ما له ، ثم إذا صح له هذا يكون مرجعه منه إليه ،

ITQAN:v1p26/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p26/r1.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p26/r1.claim: Al-Zarkashī’s inventory of Qur’anic sciences includes abrogation, ambiguous and decisive verses, divine attributes, inimitability, transmitted recitation, the Sunnah’s support, exegesis, forms of address, literal and figurative language, allusion, styles, and particles.
ITQAN:v1p26/r1.anchor: الرابع والثلاثون معرفة ناسخه ومنسوخه الخامس والثلاثون معرفة موهم المختلف السادس والثلاثون معرفة المحكم من المتشابه

ITQAN:v1p26/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p26/r2.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p26/r2.claim: Al-Zarkashī says exhaustive treatment of any field would consume a lifetime; his book therefore gives core principles and selected chapters because the discipline is long and life short.
ITQAN:v1p26/r2.anchor: واعلم أنه ما من نوع من هذه الأنواع إلا ولو أراد الإنسان استقصاءه لاستفرغ عمره ثم لم يحكم أمره

ITQAN:v1p26/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p26/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p26/r3.claim: Al-Suyuti says reading al-Burhān inspired him to complete al-Itqān; he reordered and expanded its topics and made it an introduction to his planned major tafsir, Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn wa Maṭlaʿ al-Badrayn.
ITQAN:v1p26/r3.anchor: ولما وقفت على هذا الكتاب ازددت به سرورا وحمدت الله كثيرا وقوي العزم على إبراز ما أضمرته

ITQAN:v4p325#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r1.claim: The Qurʾān is exempt from metered poetry because it is a source of truth, while poetry characteristically imagines falsehood as truth and exaggerates praise, blame, and harm; God therefore exonerated His Prophet from it.
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r1.anchor: أن القرآن منبع الحق ومجمع الصدق وقصارى أمر الشاعر التخييل بتصور الباطل في صورة الحق والإفراط في الإطراء

ITQAN:v4p325#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r2.speaker: بعض الحكماء
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r2.claim: Some sages said that no devout person who speaks truth fluently was an accomplished poet.
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض الحكماء لم ير متدين صادق اللهجة مفلقا في شعره

ITQAN:v4p325#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r3.claim: Qurʾānic phrases that happen to resemble meter are not poetry, since poetry requires deliberate intent; otherwise anyone whose speech accidentally scans would be a poet, and eloquent Arabs would have challenged it as poetry.
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r3.anchor: ولو كان شعرا لكان كل من اتفق له في كلامه شيء موزون شاعرا فكان الناس كلهم شعراء

ITQAN:v4p325#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r4.claim: One reported view says a single line, or speech matching its meter, is not poetry; poetry begins at two lines or more.
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r4.anchor: وقيل البيت الواحد وما كان على وزنه لا يسمى شعرا وأقل الشعر بيتان فصاعدا

ITQAN:v4p325#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r5.claim: Another view says rajaz is never poetry; a further view makes four lines the minimum for rajaz, and neither form occurs in the Qurʾān.
ITQAN:v4p325#2/r5.anchor: وقيل الرجز لا يسمى شعرا أصلا وقيل أقل ما يكون من الرجز شعرا أربعة أبيات وليس ذلك في القرآن بحال

ITQAN:v2p528/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p528/r1.claim: Suyūṭī lists major Qurʾānic parsing works: Makkī, al-Ḥawfī, Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī, al-Samīn, al-Safāqisī, and Abū Ḥayyān, assessing their clarity, stature, or verbosity.
ITQAN:v2p528/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف خلائق منهم مكي وكتابه في المشكل خاصة والحوفي وهو أوضحها وأبو البقاء العكبري

ITQAN:v2p528/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p528/r2.claim: Parsing is useful because it distinguishes meanings and reveals speakers’ purposes.
ITQAN:v2p528/r2.anchor: ومن فوائد هذا النوع معرفة المعنى لأن الإعراب يميز المعاني ويوقف على أغراض المتكلمين

ITQAN:v2p528/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ITQAN:v2p528/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayd reports ʿUmar urging people to learn grammatical correctness, inheritance law, and Sunna as they learn the Qurʾān.
ITQAN:v2p528/r3.anchor: أخرج أبو عبيد في فضائله عن عمر بن الخطاب قال تعلموا اللحن والفرائض والسنن كما تعلمون القرآن

ITQAN:v2p528/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r4.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v2p528/r4.claim: Yaḥyā b. ʿAtīq reports that al-Ḥasan approved learning Arabic for eloquence and sound recitation, warning that a reader may perish by failing to parse a verse.
ITQAN:v2p528/r4.anchor: قلت للحسن يا أبا سعيد الرجل يتعلم العربية يلتمس بها حسن المنطق ويقيم بها قراءته قال حسن يا بن أخي

ITQAN:v2p528/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p528/r5.claim: A reader probing the Qurʾān should examine each word’s form and syntactic position, including whether it begins speech or occurs in a reply.
ITQAN:v2p528/r5.anchor: وعلى الناظر في كتاب الله تعالى الكاشف عن أسراره النظر في الكلمة وصيغتها ومحلها ككونها مبتدأ أو خبرا

ITQAN:v2p528/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p528/r6.claim: Understand a word or construction before parsing it, since parsing follows meaning; on the view that disconnected sūra openings are unknown mysteries, they cannot be parsed.
ITQAN:v2p528/r6.anchor: أن يفهم معنى ما يريد أن يعربه مفردا أو مركبا قبل الإعراب فإنه فرع المعنى ولهذا لا يجوز إعراب فواتح السور

ITQAN:v2p535/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p535/r1.claim: Avoid calling anything in the Qurʾān زائد, since that can imply it has no meaning; alternatives include emphasis, connective particle, or insertion.
ITQAN:v2p535/r1.anchor: أن يجتنب إطلاق لفظ الزائد في كتاب الله تعالى فإن الزائد قد يفهم منه أنه لا معنى له وكتاب الله منزه عن ذلك

ITQAN:v2p535/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535/r2.speaker: ابن الخشاب
ITQAN:v2p535/r2.claim: Ibn al-Khashshāb says most scholars allow calling a Qurʾānic element زائد because this follows Arab usage: addition, like omission, has a rhetorical role such as emphasis or preparation.
ITQAN:v2p535/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الخشاب اختلف في جواز إطلاق لفظ الزائد في القرآن فالأكثرون على جوازه نظرا إلى أنه نزل بلسان القوم

ITQAN:v2p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535/r3.speaker: منهم من أبى ذلك
ITQAN:v2p535/r3.claim: Some reject the label زائد because the words so described carry particular benefits and meanings.
ITQAN:v2p535/r3.anchor: ومنهم من أبى ذلك وقال هذه الألفاظ المحمولة على الزيادة جاءت لفوائد ومعان تخصها

ITQAN:v2p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535/r4.speaker: ابن الخشاب
ITQAN:v2p535/r4.claim: Ibn al-Khashshāb resolves that an element cannot be truly needless, since that would be pointless; it is needed, though perhaps less than the word it supplements.
ITQAN:v2p535/r4.anchor: والتحقيق أنه إن أريد بالزيادة إثبات معنى لا حاجة إليه فباطل لأنه عبث فتعين أن إلينا به حاجة

ITQAN:v2p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p535/r5.claim: Suyūṭī argues that the supposedly added element is as necessary as its base for eloquence: omitting it leaves the utterance rhetorically deficient even if its basic meaning remains.
ITQAN:v2p535/r5.anchor: بل الحاجة إليه كالحاجة إليه سواء بالنظر إلى مقتضى الفصاحة والبلاغة وأنه لو ترك كان الكلام دونه

TUSTARI:11:88/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:88/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:88/r1.claim: One who knows evil but does not avoid it is no scholar; likewise one who knows acts of obedience but does not perform them.
TUSTARI:11:88/r1.anchor: كل عالم أعطي علم الشر، وليس هو مجانبا للشر، فليس بعالم

TUSTARI:11:88/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:11:88/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:11:88/r2.claim: Asked whom he should sit with, Sahl advised choosing someone whose actions, rather than speech, move you.
TUSTARI:11:88/r2.anchor: سأل رجل سهلا فقال: يا أبا محمد، إلى من تأمرني أن أجلس إليه؟

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r1.claim: The author treats circumstantial clauses here: they may occur with or without و, and he distinguishes when each form is appropriate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r1.anchor: وأول ما ينبغي أن يضبط من أمرها أنها تجيء تارة مع الواو ، وأخرى بغير الواو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r2.claim: A nominal circumstantial clause usually has و; when its subject is the pronoun of the person in the circumstantial state, omitting و is wholly unacceptable.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r2.anchor: فإن كان المبتدأ من الجملة ضمير ذي الحال لم يصلح بغير الواو البتة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r3.claim: Waw omission is common when the nominal clause has a preposed adverbial predicate such as عليه سيف; the cited poets show this usage, which the author says cannot take و in these examples.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r3.anchor: فإن كان الخبر في الجملة من المبتدأ والخبر ظرفا ، ثم كان قد قدم على المبتدأ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r4.claim: Waw is also omitted occasionally when the predicate is not a preposed adverbial, as in the cited idioms; this use is uncommon.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p160/r4.anchor: وقد يجيء ترك الواو فيما ليس الخبر فيه كذلك ، ولكنه لا يكثر

DAMGHANI:v1p282/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r5.claim: In Shuʿayb’s statement, reform means doing good.
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r5.anchor: الاصلاح الاحسان قوله سبحانه في سورة هود ان اريد الا الاصلاح ما استطعت يعني الاحسان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r1.claim: Ṣalāḥ is a change toward a sound, upright state, and its opposite is corruption.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r1.anchor: الصلاح التغير إلى الاستقامة في الحال . وضده : الفساد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r2.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r2.claim: Thaʿlab says the verb ṣaluḥa is pronounced with fatḥa on its lām.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r2.anchor: وقال ثعلب : يقال صلح الشيء بفتح اللام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt allows ṣalaḥa and ṣaluḥa, with either fatḥa or ḍamma on the lām.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت : صلح وصلح بفتحها وضمها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r4.claim: The verbal noun ṣulūḥ derives from ṣaluḥa; a cited verse asks what goodness remains after one’s parents have been insulted.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r9.claim: A fifth sense is beneficence: Shuyayb says he seeks reform as far as he can.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p396#2/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الصلاح في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r1.claim: In ordinary usage a wakīl is entrusted to manage a matter under agency; the principal must be alive, while a manager for the dead is an executor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r1.anchor: الوكيل : في العرف من قلد النظر بحكم الوكالة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r2.claim: Tawakkul is displaying one’s incapacity and relying on another; wākl means neglecting one’s affair through reliance, and wakl describes weakness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p607/r2.anchor: والتوكل : إظهار العجز والاعتماد على الغير ، وواكل فلان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r1.claim: The Qur’an uses Arabic modes of brevity, omission, emphasis, allusion, and concealment as well as explicit explanation and parable.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r1.anchor: فالجواب عنه: أن القرآن نزل بألفاظ العرب ومعانيها، ومذاهبها في الإيجاز والاختصار، والإطالة والتوكيد،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r2.claim: If every passage were equally transparent to learned and unlearned readers, human distinction and moral testing would disappear; need stimulates thought and ingenuity.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r2.anchor: ولو كان القرآن كله ظاهرا مكشوفا حتى يستوي في معرفته العالم والجاهل، لبطل التفاضل بين الناس، وسقطت المحنة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r3.claim: Sciences have difficult and subtle levels that let learners advance and give scholars distinction for investigation and extraction, meriting divine reward.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r3.anchor: وكل باب من أبواب العلم: من الفقه والحساب والفرائض والنحو، فمنه ما يجل، ومنه ما يدق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r4.speaker: قالوا
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r4.claim: A common saying contrasts wealth, which breeds dullness, with poverty, which prompts resourcefulness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r4.anchor: وقالوا: عيب الغنى أنه يورث البله، وفضيلة الفقر أنه يبعث الحيلة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r5.speaker: أكثم بن صيفي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r5.claim: Aktham says he would not want every worldly matter made effortless for him, because he dislikes becoming habituated to helplessness.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r5.anchor: وقال: أكثم بن صيفي: ما يسرني أني مكفي كل أمر الدنيا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r6.claim: Subtle meanings occur across prophetic speech, Companions’ and Successors’ speech, poetry, and oratory, and may be grasped only by accomplished readers.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا المثال كلام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكلام صحابته والتابعين، وأشعار الشعراء،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r7.claim: The Prophet compares people to a hundred camels among which one can scarcely find a riding camel, illustrating the rarity of exceptional persons.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «تجدون الناس كإبل مائة ليس فيها راحلة»

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r8.claim: The Prophet says not to seek illumination from the fire of polytheists; Ibn Qutayba cites it as an example of subtle prophetic speech.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r9.claim: The Prophet warns that some spring growth kills an animal through overeating or nearly does so.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r9.anchor: وقال: «إن مما ينبت الربيع ما يقتل حبطا أو يلم»

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r10.claim: The Prophet tells al-Dahhak ibn Sufyan to settle among his people like a gazelle when he reaches them.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p58/r10.anchor: وقال للضحاك بن سفيان حين بعثه إلى قومه: «إذا أتيتهم فاربض في دارهم ظبيا»

NAHHAS:v2p298/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p298/r9.claim: Shuayb's point is, “Would I not forbid you from error?”

NAHHAS:v2p298/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p298/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p298/r10.claim: وما أريد أن أخالفكم is accusative as the complement of أريد.
NAHHAS:v2p298/r10.anchor: ( وما أريد أن أخالفكم ) في موضع نصب بأريد

SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the answer to أرأيتم is omitted, its location made clear by the Noah and Ṣāliḥ accounts: if Shuʿayb truly has proof and prophethood, he must command abandoning idols and sins, as prophets are sent to do.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r1.anchor: جوابه محذوف، وإنما لم يثبت لأن إثباته في القصتين دل على مكانه، ومعنى الكلام ينادي عليه

SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r2.claim: The Shaykh says that is not a technical answer to أرأيتم: if the verb means أخبروني, the supplied clause is its second object, normally an interrogative sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وتسمية هذا جوابا لـ " أرأيتم " ليس بالمصطلح، بل هذه الجملة التي قدرها في موضع المفعول الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r3.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r3.claim: Al-Ḥawfī takes the conditional answer as omitted and supplies أأعدل عما أنا عليه.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r3.anchor: وقال الحوفي: " وجواب الشرط محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه تقديره: أأعدل عما أنا عليه "

SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted conditional answer such as أضل كما ضللتم or أترك تبليغ الرسالة.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وجواب الشرط الذي في قوله " أن كنت " محذوف تقديره: أضل كما ضللتم

SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r5.claim: The Shaykh rejects أضل as the conditional answer: declarative wording does not follow from the condition, while an implied interrogative belongs as أرأيتم's second object; the answer is inferred from the preceding clause and its complement.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وليس قوله " أضل " جوابا للشرط؛ لأنه إن كان مثبتا فلا يمكن أن يكون جوابا

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī distinguishes خالفني إلى الشيء, when the other person goes toward it as you turn away, from خالفني عنه, when directions are reversed; Shuʿayb means he will not race to their forbidden desires to monopolize them.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " خالفني فلان إلى كذا: إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه، وخالفني عنه: إذا ولى عنه وأنت قاصده،

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r2.claim: أن أخالفكم may be the object of أريد, with form III خالف used like simple فعل; إلى ما أنهاكم attaches to أخالفكم or modifies an omitted مائلا.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r2.anchor: فأقول: يجوز أن يكون " أن أخالفكم " في موضع مفعول ب " أريد " ، أي: وما أريد مخالفتكم، ويكون فاعل بمعنى فعل

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r3.claim: Another parse makes أن أخالفكم a causal object, with إلى attached to أريد in the sense intend; the phrase means he does not aim to violate the prohibition by opposing them.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " أن أخالفكم " مفعولا من أجله، وتتعلق " إلى " بقوله " أريد " بمعنى: وما أقصد

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses the construction as not intending, by opposing them, to commit what he forbids.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#2/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال الزجاج: " وما أقصد بخلافكم إلى ارتكاب ما أنهاكم عنه.

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r1.claim: ما استطعت may be a temporal verbal noun, meaning as long as I can; a relative phrase in apposition to الإصلاح; or إصلاح ما استطعت with an omitted noun.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r1.anchor: قوله: { ما استطعت } يجوز في " ما " هذه وجوه، أحدها: أن تكون مصدرية ظرفية أي: مدة استطاعتي.

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī gives the first three parses; a fourth makes ما the direct object of the definite verbal noun, illustrated by an unnamed poetic line, though al-Samīn says this use is rare for Basrans and disallowed by Kufans.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r2.anchor: ذكر هذه الأوجه الثلاثة الزمخشري، إلا أن إعمال المصدر المعرف قليل عند البصريين،

SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r3.claim: Fronting عليه and إليه marks exclusivity: on God alone Shuʿayb relies, and to Him alone he turns.
SAMIN-DURR:11:88#3/r3.anchor: وتقدم الجاران في " عليه " و " إليه " للاختصاص أي: عليه لا على غيره، وإليه لا إلى غيره.

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r1.claim: The conditional clause has no expressed answer because its meaning is understood by the audience.

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r2.claim: One explanation of good provision is lawful provision.

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r3.claim: Another explanation is the obedience to which Shuʿayb was enabled.
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r3.anchor: وقيل:. رزقا حسنا ما وفق له

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r4.claim: Shuʿayb says he does not forbid something and then do it himself; he chooses for them what he chooses for himself.
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r4.anchor: أي لست أنهاكم عن شيء وأدخل فيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r5.claim: The construction means to aim, by acting contrary to someone, at doing the very thing one forbids.
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r5.anchor: أي ما أقصد بخلافك القصد إلى أن أرتكبه

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r6.claim: As much as he is able means his capacity to convey the warning; he cannot compel people to obey.
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r6.anchor: أي بقدر طاقتي، وقدر طاقتي إبلاغكم وإنذاركم

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r7.claim: Neither Shuʿayb nor anyone else can perform obedience except through God's enabling.
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r7.anchor: فأعلم أنه لا يقدر هو ولا غيره على الطاعة

ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p73/r8.claim: Anību means that Shuʿayb returns to God.

ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari, Razi and several other commentators
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r1.claim: Zamakhshari, Razi, and other commentators treat the bracketed clause as elliptically implied in Shu'ayb's reply.
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r1.anchor: Zamakhshari, Razi and several other commentators, the clause interpolated here between brackets is elliptically implied in Shu'ayb's answer

ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r2.claim: Shu'ayb mentions God's ample worldly gifts to show that self-interest does not motivate his demand for fair dealings.
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n122/r2.anchor: His stress on the fact that God has graced him amply with worldly goods is meant to remind his countrymen that it is not self-interest
