ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n123/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n123/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n123/r1.claim: Shu'ayb says he does not intend to deprive them of what rightfully belongs to them, referring to 11:85.
ASAD-NOTES:11:88#n123/r1.anchor: I do not aim at depriving you of what is rightfully yours

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r1.claim: She criticizes al-Baqillani and Abd al-Qahir for relying heavily on poetry in discussions of eloquence while rarely using Qur'anic examples to illuminate rhetorical points.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r1.anchor: فنرى الباقلانى مثلاً يُخرج في كتابه عن الدراسة القرآنية إلى دراسات للشعر، ونرى عبد القاهر يستكثر في (الدلائل) من الاستشهاد بالشعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الأصبع المصري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba is a rare exception: his Badi' al-Qur'an gives Qur'anic examples priority, following al-Rummani's approach.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r2.anchor: كابن أبي الأصبع المصري - في القرن السابع - الذي سار في (بديع القرآن) على نهج الرماني

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r3.claim: She follows al-Rummani's pioneering Qur'anic rhetoric, praising its clear method as free from kalam disputation and from attention to claims of successful imitation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r3.anchor: انطلاقاً من هذه الخطوة الرائدة التي وصل إليها جهد الرماني في دراسته البلاغية للقرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r4.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r4.claim: Abd al-Jabbar studies eloquence to prove the Qur'an's inimitability; for him, an unprecedented style alone is insufficient unless its level of eloquence is also considered.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r4.anchor: فصاحة القرآن كانت مناط النظر، في الجزء الخاص بإعجاز القرآن، من (كتاب المغني) للقاضي المعتزلي عبد الجبار

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r5.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r5.claim: He understands nazm as a particular mode of composition and rejects mere novelty as a sufficient proof of inimitability, since even a novel but clumsy style would then qualify.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p107/r5.anchor: والملحظ الدقيق في النظم عنده. بمعنى النسق والطريقة، أنه لا يكفي عدم السبق إلى مثله

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r1.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r1.claim: Khuli's reform method transfers modern literary criticism to Qur'anic interpretation, which he calls literary tafsir; he argues Arabs naturally approached the Quran as a supreme work of Arabic literature deserving study.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r1.anchor: كان مدخل الشيخ أمين الخولي لتجديد مناهج تفسير القرآن توظيفَ المناهج الحديثة في تفسير ونقد النصوص الأدبية، وتعميمَها لتشمل النص القرآني

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r2.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r2.claim: Khuli defines the first task of contemporary tafsir as a methodologically sound, comprehensive, consistently organized literary study, initially pursued without other considerations and made the basis for further aims.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r2.anchor: يشرح الشيخ الخولي طريقتَه في التفسير الأدبي قائلًا: «إن التفسير اليوم — فيما أفهمه — هو الدراسة الأدبية

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r3.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r3.claim: Khuli's literary method reads the Quran topic by topic rather than in mushaf order, tracing revelation contexts, organic unity, internal logic, and shared concepts that support psychological, ethical, and social reform.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r3.anchor: تبتني طريقة «التفسير الأدبي للقرآن» على تفسير الآيات في سياق موضوعات القرآن، وليس تفسيرَها على وفق ترتيبها في سور القرآن

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r4.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r4.claim: For Khuli, literary analysis serves the Quran's guidance and broad ethical and social reform; the method does not pursue art or literature for its own sake.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r4.anchor: ليست هناك آية أو كلمة تَرِد في القرآن إلا ويكون هدفُها الهدي والرحمة، وليس الهدف الأدب بوصفه أدبًا، أو الفن بوصفه فنًّا

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r5.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r5.claim: Khuli organizes literary tafsir around two dimensions: studying the Quran's setting and studying the Quran itself.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r5.anchor: يشرح الخولي ما ينشده في طريقة تفسيره الأدبي، فيؤكد أنه يتمحور حول بُعدين

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r6.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r6.claim: Study around the Quran reconstructs its material, social, and cultural setting and the first audience's tastes and habits of understanding; this synchronic approach seeks the original uptake through human, social, and language sciences.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r6.anchor: ويعني بالدراسة حول القرآن «دراسة البيئة المادية والمعنوية والثقافية التي نزل فيها القرآن الكريم.»

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r7.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r7.claim: Study of the Quran itself examines word meanings and their historical development, contact between Arabic and other Muslim languages, and how changing eras and meanings affect interpretation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r7.anchor: أما البعد الثاني لتفسيره الأدبي وهو دراسة القرآن ذاته، فيريد به شرح الكلمات، وبيان معاني المفردات، والكشف عن طبيعةِ حياة الألفاظ وتطور دلالتها عبر الزمان

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r8.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r8.claim: Al-Rifai explains that Khuli adds a psychological dimension: psychological inimitability is the Quran's powerful effect on human beings, their experience of its eloquence, and their response to it, studied with psychology.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r8.anchor: وحدد مفهوم «الإعجاز النفسي لبلاغة القرآنِ الكريم؛ بمعنى أثرِه العظيم على النفس الإنسانية ووقْعه عليها وفعله فيها.

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r9.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r9.claim: Al-Rifai presents psychological tafsir as Khuli's disciplined way to explain brevity, elaboration, emphasis, allusion, generality, detail, repetition, arrangement, and coherence; other explanations risk contrivance.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r9.anchor: فبالأمور النفسية لا غير، يعلَّل إيجازُه وإطنابُه، وتوكيدُه وإشارتُه، وإجمالُه وتفصيلُه، وتكرارُه وإطالتُه

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r10.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r10.claim: Al-Rifai says Khuli warned against claiming that the Quran anticipated scientific discoveries or extracting modern psychology from it; psychological research should instead help explain the Quran's psychological effect.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r10.anchor: تنبه الشيخ الخولي مبكرًا إلى خطأ الزعم بسبق القرآنِ لاكتشافات العِلْم ومكاسبِه، أو الاشتغال على إسقاط هذه الاكتشافات على الآيات الكريمة

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r11.claim: Al-Rifai criticizes projects such as Islamic psychology, sociology, and economics as wasteful efforts to make religious identity catch up with modern science through an unwarranted Islamization of knowledge.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r11.anchor: العمل على خلط الدين بالعلم، وإهدار طاقات الكثير من الباحثين الشباب، وتضييع عقولهم في متاهات بناء: علم نفس إسلامي، وعلم اجتماع إسلامي

RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r12.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r12.claim: Al-Rifai credits second-generation scholar Nasr Hamid Abu Zayd with developing Khuli's school through the use of hermeneutics in Qur'anic interpretation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c4/r12.anchor: وواصل الجيل الثاني، ممثلًا بنصر حامد أبو زيد، نهج «مدرسة الأمناء» التي شَاد لبناتها الفكرية أمين الخولي

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r4.claim: Fronting the prepositional phrase with trust and turning to God signals exclusivity: reliance is on Him alone, and turning back is only to Him.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r4.anchor: فقدم الجار والمجرور للدلالة على الاختصاص وذلك لأن التوكل لا يكون إلا على الله وحده

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: Sibawayh prefers raising generic nouns after أما because ordinary nouns do not behave like verbal nouns; أما العبيد فذو عبيد means one has a share among the slaves.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: ما ذكرت فى هذا باب أسماء والأسماء لا تجرى مجرى المصادر

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: The raised construction can be understood with an omitted preposition and phrase: أما من العبيد or أما في العبيد فأنت ذو عبيد.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: أما العبيد فأنت فيهم أو أنت منهم

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: أما ابن مزنية فأنا ابن مزنية can identify the second expression with the first; when the noun is circumstantial, accusative is also possible, as in صديقا or صاحبا.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: أما ابن مزنية فأنا ابن مزنية

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: Sibawayh allows accusative after أما when it is a circumstantial, as in أما صديقا فأنت صديق and أما صاحبا فأنت صاحب.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: كما قلت أما صديقا فأنت صديق

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: Yunus reports that some Arabs treat العبيد and العبد after أما like verbal nouns, yielding an accusative construction.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: وزعم يونس أن قوما من العرب يقولون

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: Sibawayh calls that usage rare and bad; the proper construction is raised, as Arabs, Abu Amr, and Yunus say, and he knows of no disagreement from al-Khalil.

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: Applying the accusative analysis to أما العلم والعبيد is also ugly: it treats ordinary nouns as verbal nouns even though each alone should be raised.

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: When أما introduces a known, definite referent such as al-Harith or specific slaves, only raising works; the expression means there is no one of that identity beyond or apart from the known referent.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: فهذا لا يكون فيه أبدا إلا الرفع

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: أما أبوك فلك أب is likewise raised, understood as having a father in relation to or in the person of your father; accusative is unavailable.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: فهذا لا يكون فيه أبدا إلا الرفع

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: أن plus its verb functions like a verbal noun in أما أن يكون عالما; the verse's أن أخالفكم is likewise an infinitival complement. Sibawayh cites لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب as parallel evidence.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: أن مع الفعل الذى يكون صلة بمنزلة المصدر

SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.claim: The أن clause is not circumstantial: it refers to what is to happen afterward, rather than describing the first event as it occurs.
SIBAWAYH:وزعميونسأنهقولأبىعمرو|وذلكقولكأ.anchor: ولا تقع أن وصلتها حالا يكون الأول فى حال وقوعه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r1.claim: Ibn Masud urges readers to follow inherited practice and not invent, saying they have been given what suffices.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال اتبعوا ولا تبتدعوا فقد كفيتم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r2.speaker: حذيفة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r2.claim: Hudhayfa tells Qur'an readers to follow predecessors: remaining on their path is advance, while turning aside is deep misguidance.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r2.anchor: قال حذيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه اتقوا الله يا معشر القراء وخذوا طريق من كان قبلكم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r3.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet commanded them to recite the Qur'an as they had been taught.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r3.anchor: عن زر عن عبد الله قال قال لنا علي بن أبي طالب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says reciters' readings were close, instructs them to recite as taught, avoid affectation and dispute, and likens variants to equivalent expressions.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r4.anchor: قال عبد الله إني سمعت القرأة فرأيتم متقاربين فاقرءوا كما علمتم وإياكم والتنطع والاختلاف وإنما هو كقولك هلم وأقبل وتعال

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r5.claim: Ibn Mujahid presents Abu Amr as a leading linguist and reader who learned from major Successors and would not recite without prior precedent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r5.anchor: وقد كان أبو عمرو بن العلاء وهو إمام أهل عصره في اللغة وقد رأس في القراءة والتابعون أحياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r6.claim: Abu Amr says that, if not bound to readings already recited, he would have chosen some other letter forms, which the passage leaves unspecified.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا عمرو بن العلاء يقول لولا أنه ليس لي أن أقرأ إلا بما قد قرىء به لقرأت حرف كذا كذا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r7.claim: Asked whether the alternatives باركنا عليه and تركنا عليه could be recognized, Abu Amr says they are known only by hearing them from the early teachers.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p46/r7.anchor: حدثنا ابن أخي الأصمعي عن عمه قال قلت لأبي عمرو

NASHR:v2p292/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p292/r8.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
NASHR:v2p292/r8.claim: The Medinans, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir open the yāʾ in وما توفيقي إلا بالله.
NASHR:v2p292/r8.anchor: وما توفيقي إلا بالله فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وابن عامر

NASHR:v1p207/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p207/r1.claim: Tadwir is the middle pace between full realization and rapid recitation; most authorities use it when transmitting separated-lengthening without full extension, and it is the preferred practice of most performance specialists.
NASHR:v1p207/r1.anchor: وأما التدوير فهو عبارة عن التوسط بين المقامين من التحقيق والحدر

NASHR:v1p207/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASHR:v1p207/r2.claim: Ibn Masud warns against scattering the Quran like low-grade dates or reciting it hastily like poetry.
NASHR:v1p207/r2.anchor: قال ابن مسعود - رضي الله عنه -: لا تنثروه - يعني القرآن - نثر الدقل ولا تهذوه هذ الشعر.

NASHR:v1p207/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p207/r3.claim: Tartil means letting speech follow in measured succession with reflection and understanding rather than haste; it is the manner in which the Quran was revealed.
NASHR:v1p207/r3.anchor: وأما الترتيل فهو مصدر من رتل فلان كلامه إذا أتبع بعضه بعضا على مكث وتفهم

NASHR:v1p207/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v1p207/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command to recite in tartil as making the recitation clear.
NASHR:v1p207/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بينه. وقال مجاهد: تأن فيه. وقال الضحاك: انبذه حرفا حرفا.

NASHR:v1p207/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r5.speaker: مجاهد
NASHR:v1p207/r5.claim: Mujahid explains tartil as taking time over the recitation.
NASHR:v1p207/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: تأن فيه. وقال الضحاك: انبذه حرفا حرفا. يقول تعالى تلبث في قراءته وتمهل فيها

NASHR:v1p207/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r6.speaker: الضحاك
NASHR:v1p207/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak explains tartil as articulating the Quran one letter at a time; the author says the command and emphatic verbal noun encourage reflection and understanding.
NASHR:v1p207/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: انبذه حرفا حرفا. يقول تعالى تلبث في قراءته وتمهل فيها، وافصل الحرف من الحرف الذي بعده

NASHR:v1p207/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r7.speaker: أم سلمة
NASHR:v1p207/r7.claim: Umm Salama described the Prophet’s recitation as carefully articulated, letter by letter.
NASHR:v1p207/r7.anchor: عن يعلى بن مالك أنه سأل أم سلمة - رضي الله عنها -

NASHR:v1p207/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r8.speaker: عائشة
NASHR:v1p207/r8.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet would recite a sura until it became longer than another sura.
NASHR:v1p207/r8.anchor: قالت عائشة - رضي الله عنها -: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

NASHR:v1p207/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r9.speaker: أبو الدرداء
NASHR:v1p207/r9.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that the Prophet repeated “If You punish them, they are Your servants” in prayer until morning.
NASHR:v1p207/r9.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء - رضي الله عنه - أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قام بآية يرددها حتى أصبح إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك

NASHR:v1p207/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p207/r10.speaker: أنس
NASHR:v1p207/r10.claim: Anas said the Prophet’s recitation used lengthening and demonstrated it by prolonging the divine names in the basmala; the author concludes that full realization falls within tartil.
NASHR:v1p207/r10.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري عن أنس أنه سئل عن قراءة رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم - فقال: كانت مدا،

NASHR:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p248/r1.claim: The transmitted formula for seeking refuge is “أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم”; the Prophet was taught that wording, and the author argues that he and his Companions did not replace it with “أستعيذ”.
NASHR:v1p248/r1.anchor: والقصد أن الذي تواتر عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في التعوذ للقراءة ولسائر تعوذاته

NASHR:v1p248/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p248/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
NASHR:v1p248/r2.claim: A report in Abu Awana relates that the Prophet taught seeking refuge from the Fire, trials, and the Dajjal; the Companions answered with the wording “نعوذ بالله”.
NASHR:v1p248/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح أبي عوانة عن زيد بن ثابت - رضي الله عنه - أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أقبل علينا

NASHR:v1p248/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p248/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p248/r3.claim: The author argues the Prophet explicitly taught the formula “اللهم إني أعوذ بك” for seeking refuge from four matters, leaving no wording more explicit.
NASHR:v1p248/r3.anchor: إذا تشهد أحدكم فليستعذ بالله من أربع: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب جهنم

NASHR:v1p248/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p248/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
NASHR:v1p248/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin is reported to have used “أعوذ بالسميع العليم”; some restricted this form to voluntary prayer, and its transmission from Hamza is questioned by the author.
NASHR:v1p248/r4.anchor: وأما بالله) فقد جاء عن ابن سيرين: أعوذ بالسميع العليم، وقيده بعضهم بصلاة التطوع

NASHR:v1p391/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p391/r1.claim: Al-Azraq changes a silent hamza when it is the first radical of a verb, with examples, but exempts forms from the awā root; he changes only the listed medial forms and realizes other hamzas.
NASHR:v1p391/r1.anchor: وأما من طريق الأزرق، فإنه يبدل الهمزة إذا وقعت فاء من الفعل نحو (يومنون، ويالمون، وياخذ

NASHR:v1p391/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r2.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p391/r2.claim: Al-Dani says Abu Amr did not pronounce silent hamza during prayer, rapid recitation, or major assimilation; other manuals limit the rule to prayer or rapid recitation.
NASHR:v1p391/r2.anchor: وذلك أن الداني قال في " التيسير ": اعلم أن أبا عمرو كان إذا قرأ في الصلاة

NASHR:v1p391/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p391/r3.claim: Reports from al-Yazidi’s transmitters disagree: some say Abu Amr dropped jussive hamzas in rapid recitation but realized them when slow, while another says he dropped them in prayer only.
NASHR:v1p391/r3.anchor: قال في " جامع البيان ": اختلف أصحاب اليزيدي عنه في الحال التي يستعمل ترك الهمز فيها

NASHR:v1p391/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r4.speaker: الدوري
NASHR:v1p391/r4.claim: Other transmitters from al-Duri report that Abu Amr never pronounced hamza, in prayer or outside it and at either rapid or measured pace.
NASHR:v1p391/r4.anchor: وحكى أبو عبد الرحمن، وإبراهيم في رواية العباس وأبو حمدون وأبو خلاد ومحمد بن شجاع،

NASHR:v1p391/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p391/r5.claim: Idraj means rapid recitation, the opposite of full realization, not connected recitation as opposed to pausing; the author rejects the resulting claim that Abu Amr changes hamza only in connection and realizes it at pause.
NASHR:v1p391/r5.anchor: والمقصود بالإدراج هو الإسراع، وهو ضد التحقيق، لا كما فهمه من لا فهم له

NASHR:v1p391/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r6.speaker: أبو العلاء
NASHR:v1p391/r6.claim: Abu al-Ala gives Abu Amr two approaches: full realization with clear articulation and easing with assimilation, or easing with clear articulation alone; this excludes full realization with assimilation.
NASHR:v1p391/r6.anchor: وقال الحافظ أبو العلاء: وأما أبو عمرو فله مذهبان: أحدهما التحقيق مع الإظهار والتخفيف مع الإدغام

NASHR:v1p391/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p391/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p391/r7.claim: Performance authorities agree on fifteen words in thirty-five positions exempted from the general replacement rule reported from Abu Amr, grouped into five categories.
NASHR:v1p391/r7.anchor: واعلم أن الأئمة من أهل الأداء أجمعوا عمن روى البدل عن أبي عمرو على استثناء خمس عشرة كلمة

NASHR:v2p146/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r1.speaker: أبو العز
NASHR:v2p146/r1.claim: Abu al-Izz alone reports, through al-Qadi Abu al-Ala from Ruways, pausing on “ما”; other cited manuals do not mention this point.
NASHR:v2p146/r1.anchor: وانفرد أيضا أبو العز فذكر في كفايته الوقف على (ما) كذلك من طريق القاضي أبي العلاء

NASHR:v2p146/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p146/r2.claim: Because the written lam of preposition is separated from what follows, some allow pausing on the lam by orthographic analogy; others disallow it because a prepositional lam cannot be severed syntactically.
NASHR:v2p146/r2.anchor: وهذه الكلمات قد كتبت لام الجر فيها مفصولة مما بعدها فيحتمل عند هؤلاء الوقف عليها

NASHR:v2p146/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p146/r3.claim: The author favors pausing on “ما” for these readers because it is separate in pronunciation, syntax, and script, and no explicit report contradicts that practice.
NASHR:v2p146/r3.anchor: وأما الواقف على (ما) عند هؤلاء فيجوز، بلا نظر عندهم على الجميع للانفصال لفظا وحكما ورسما

NASHR:v2p146/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p146/r4.claim: Two sound transmission routes establish that al-Kisai paused both on “ما” and on the lam.
NASHR:v2p146/r4.anchor: أما الكسائي، فقد ثبت عنه الوقف على (ما) ، وعلى اللام من طريقين صحيحين

NASHR:v2p146/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p146/r5.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman and Ibrahim ibn al-Yazidi explicitly transmit Abu Amr’s pause on “ما”; this does not rule out pausing on the lam, and no explicit report survives from al-Duri or al-Susi.
NASHR:v2p146/r5.anchor: وأما أبو عمرو فجاء عنه بالنص على الوقف على (ما) أبو عبد الرحمن وإبراهيم بنا اليزيدي

NASHR:v2p146/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r6.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p146/r6.claim: Al-Dani says no explicit report exists for the other readers, so following the written form would entail pausing on the lam; the author questions this inference because the same script also permits pausing on “ما”.
NASHR:v2p146/r6.anchor: الباقون، فقد صرح الداني في جامعه بعدم النص عنهم فقال: وليس عن الباقين في ذلك نص سوى ما جاء

NASHR:v2p146/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p146/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p146/r7.claim: Reports for Warsh allow both pauses: al-Azraq pauses on the lam while Abd al-Samad drops the lam and pauses on “ما”; the author extends both options to other readers.
NASHR:v2p146/r7.anchor: وكان عبد الصمد يقف على فما ويطرح اللام انتهى. فدل هذا على جواز الوجهين جميعا عنه

NASHR:v2p185/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p185/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p185/r1.claim: Some report deleting the yā in both positions, but the author knows no explicit route in his books; it appears in al-Tajrid via al-Hulwani and is explicit from several transmitters from Hisham.
NASHR:v2p185/r1.anchor: وروى بعضهم عنه الحذف في الحالين، ولا أعلمه نصا من طرق كتابنا لأحد من أئمتنا

NASHR:v2p185/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p185/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p185/r2.claim: The author accepts both forms as sound from Hisham in pause, but follows only retention of the yā in connected recitation through his transmission routes.
NASHR:v2p185/r2.anchor: وكلا الوجهين صحيحان عنه نصا وأداء حالة الوقف

NASHR:v2p185/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p185/r3.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p185/r3.claim: Some authorities transmit retention of the yā in connected recitation from Ibn Dhakwan; Ibn Balima gives it as the sole form, while other manuals report deletion in both positions or retention in connection.
NASHR:v2p185/r3.anchor: وروى بعض أئمتنا إثبات الياء فيها وصلا عن ابن ذكوان، وهو الذي في تلخيص ابن بليمة

NASHR:v2p185/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p185/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p185/r4.claim: Retention from Ibn Dhakwan is traced through Ahmad ibn Yusuf to Abd al-Hamid ibn Bakkar and the Syrian codex; deletion is the established practice and the author adopts it.
NASHR:v2p185/r4.anchor: والحذف عن ابن ذكوان هو الذي عليه العمل، وبه آخذ والله تعالى الموفق

NASHR:v2p185/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p185/r5.speaker: ابن شنبوذ
NASHR:v2p185/r5.claim: Some report retaining eight yā additions from Ibn Shanabudh via Qunbul, but their accounts conflict over whether particular forms are retained in connection alone or in both positions.
NASHR:v2p185/r5.anchor: وروى بعضهم أيضا إثبات الياء في هذه المواضع الثمانية عن ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل واضطربوا عنه

NASHR:v2p285/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r1.speaker: رويس
NASHR:v2p285/r1.claim: Ruways reads “فليفرحوا” as direct address, a reading also attributed to Ubay and transmitted from the Prophet; the other readers use third-person form.
NASHR:v2p285/r1.anchor: فروى رويس بالخطاب، وهي قراءة أبي، ورويناهما مسندة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهي لغة لبعض العرب

NASHR:v2p285/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
NASHR:v2p285/r2.claim: A sound hadith through Ubay ibn Kab says the Prophet recited the verse in Yunus with direct address in both verbs: “فلتفرحوا” and “تجمعون”.
NASHR:v2p285/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قرأ قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فلتفرحوا

NASHR:v2p285/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p285/r3.claim: In “مما يجمعون,” Abu Jafar, Ibn Amir, and Ruways read with direct address; the rest read in the third person.
NASHR:v2p285/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالغيب واختلفوا في مما يجمعون فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر ورويس بالخطاب

NASHR:v2p285/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NASHR:v2p285/r4.claim: Al-Kisai reads “وما يعزب” with kasra on zāy, while the others use damma; the same difference occurs in Saba.
NASHR:v2p285/r4.anchor: (واختلفوا) في: وما يعزب هنا، وفي سبأ فقرأ الكسائي بكسر الزاي، وقرأ الباقون بضمها.

NASHR:v2p285/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r5.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p285/r5.claim: Yaqub, Hamza, and Khalaf read both “ولا أصغر ولا أكبر” with nominative rā; the others use accusative, while all readers use nominative for the two forms in Saba because “مثقال” is nominative.
NASHR:v2p285/r5.anchor: (واختلفوا) في: ولا أصغر، ولا أكبر فقرأ يعقوب وحمزة وخلف برفع الراء فيهما، وقرأ الباقون بالنصب.

NASHR:v2p285/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r6.speaker: رويس
NASHR:v2p285/r6.claim: Ruways has a reading of “فأجمعوا” with hamzat wasl and fatḥa on mīm, transmitted by several routes and preferred for him by Abu al-Ala despite contrary reports; it is also attributed to Asim al-Jahdari and others.
NASHR:v2p285/r6.anchor: عن رويس في فأجمعوا، فروى أبو الطيب والقاضي أبو العلاء عن النخاس كلاهما عن التمار

NASHR:v2p285/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p285/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p285/r7.claim: The reading is an imperative from jamaʿa, opposite to separating; some say jamaʿa and ajmaʿa are synonymous, supported by the verse about gathering a plot and coming forward.
NASHR:v2p285/r7.anchor: وهي أمر: من جمع، ضد فرق، قال تعالى: فجمع كيده ثم أتى وقيل: جمع وأجمع بمعنى

NASHR:v2p457/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r1.speaker: البيهقي
NASHR:v2p457/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet gathered his family when completing the Quran, but al-Bayhaqi judges the marfu attribution mistaken; the sound version is mawquf from Anas.
NASHR:v2p457/r1.anchor: وروينا عنه في حديث مرفوع، ولفظه: أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا ختم القرآن

NASHR:v2p457/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r2.speaker: مجاهد
NASHR:v2p457/r2.claim: The early Muslims recommended gathering pious and learned people for a completion; Mujahid invited the speaker to join a completion with Ibn Abi Lubaba, then supplicated when they finished, since prayer at completion was thought to be answered.
NASHR:v2p457/r2.anchor: فقد روينا عن شعبة عن الحكم قال: أرسل إلي مجاهد، وعنده ابن أبي لبابة قال: إنما أرسلنا إليك

NASHR:v2p457/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r3.speaker: السلف
NASHR:v2p457/r3.claim: Many early Muslims preferred completing the Quran on Monday or Friday night; some chose fasting, iftar, early night, or early day, and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad said a daytime or nighttime completion brought forgiveness for that period.
NASHR:v2p457/r3.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن الأسود: من قرأ القرآن فختمه نهارا غفر له ذلك اليوم

NASHR:v2p457/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r4.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
NASHR:v2p457/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi reports the saying that angels pray for a person who completes the Quran for the remainder of that day and night; people therefore favored finishing just before day or night.
NASHR:v2p457/r4.anchor: وعن إبراهيم التيمي أنه قال: كانوا يقولون إذا ختم الرجل القرآن صلت عليه الملائكة بقية يومه وبقية ليلته

NASHR:v2p457/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p457/r5.claim: The author recommends choosing blessed and answerable times, places, and circumstances to gather the causes of an accepted supplication; Quran completion is a noble, witnessed time, especially with sound connected recitation.
NASHR:v2p457/r5.anchor: ولا شك أن وقت ختم القرآن وقت شريف وساعته ساعة مشهودة، ولاسيما ختمة قرئت قراءة صحيحة مرضية كما أنزلها الله تعالى

NASHR:v2p457/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p457/r6.claim: Supplication should be sincere without ostentation or desire for reputation, as commanded in the cited verses.
NASHR:v2p457/r6.anchor: منها: أن يقصد الله تبارك وتعالى بدعائه غير رياء، ولا سمعة قال تعالى فادعوه مخلصين له الدين وقال تعالى فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين

NASHR:v2p457/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p457/r7.claim: One should precede supplication with a good deed such as charity, supported by the accepted account of three people trapped in a cave whose boulder moved after they invoked their deeds.
NASHR:v2p457/r7.anchor: ومنها: تقديم عمل صالح من صدقة، أو غيرها للحديث المجمع على صحته حديث الثلاثة الذين أووا إلى الغار

NASHR:v2p457/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p457/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p457/r8.claim: The author advises avoiding unlawful food, drink, clothing, and earnings, citing Abu Hurayra’s report about the traveler whose supplication is obstructed by what is unlawful.
NASHR:v2p457/r8.anchor: ومنها: تجنب الحرام أكلا وشربا ولبسا وكسبا لحديث أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذكر الرجل يطيل السفر

NASHR:v2p458/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p458/r1.claim: A Muslim report warns that a traveler whose food, drink, clothing, and nourishment are unlawful may call upon God without being answered.
NASHR:v2p458/r1.anchor: يمد يديه إلى السماء يا رب يا رب ومطعمه حرام ومشربه حرام وملبسه حرام وغذي بالحرام فأنى يستجاب لذلك؟ رواه مسلم.

NASHR:v2p458/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r2.speaker: عثمان بن حنيف
NASHR:v2p458/r2.claim: In the report of the blind man who asked the Prophet to pray for his cure, he chose supplication over patience and was instructed to perform ablution well and pray.
NASHR:v2p458/r2.anchor: لحديث عثمان بن حنيف رضي الله عنه أن رجلا ضرير البصر أتى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

NASHR:v2p458/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NASHR:v2p458/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet faced the Kaaba and prayed against several Quraysh leaders; it is agreed upon, and many reports support facing the qibla.
NASHR:v2p458/r3.anchor: لحديث عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه: استقبل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الكعبة فدعا على نفر

NASHR:v2p458/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r4.speaker: سليمان
NASHR:v2p458/r4.claim: A Prophetic report describes God as generous and forbearing toward a servant who raises his hands, not returning them empty.
NASHR:v2p458/r4.anchor: لحديث سليمان يرفعه (إن ربكم حيي كريم يستحيي من عبده إذا رفع يديه إلى السماء أن يردهما صفرا)

NASHR:v2p458/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p458/r5.claim: A Prophetic report describes supplication as raising the hands level with the shoulders or near that height.
NASHR:v2p458/r5.anchor: وحديث ابن عباس أنه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: (المسألة أن ترفع يديك حذو منكبيك، أو نحوهما)

NASHR:v2p458/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r6.speaker: علي
NASHR:v2p458/r6.claim: Ali reports that raising the hands is the humility and entreaty named in 23:76.
NASHR:v2p458/r6.anchor: ولحديث علي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: (رفع اليدين من الاستكانة

NASHR:v2p458/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن جعفر
NASHR:v2p458/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet gathered his family beneath a cloak, raised his hands, and prayed, God, these are my family.
NASHR:v2p458/r7.anchor: ولحديث عبد الله بن جعفر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لما جمع أهل بيته

NASHR:v2p458/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r8.speaker: الخطابي
NASHR:v2p458/r8.claim: Al-Khattabi considers it proper etiquette to leave the hands uncovered while raising them in supplication.
NASHR:v2p458/r8.anchor: قال الخطابي إن من الأدب أن تكون اليدان في حالة رفعهما مكشوفين غير مغطاتين

NASHR:v2p458/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p458/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
NASHR:v2p458/r9.claim: Abu Sulayman covered one hand against the cold during prayer, left the other extended, then saw the exposed hand adorned.
NASHR:v2p458/r9.anchor: (قلت) : روينا عن أبي سليمان الداراني رحمة الله عليه قال: كنت ليلة باردة في المحراب

NASHR:v2p25/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p25/r1.claim: Jaʿfar transmits retained ghunna for Khalaf from Hamza; al-Muhaj gives both options, and the author judges both sound.
NASHR:v2p25/r1.anchor: كرواية خلف عن حمزة. وروى عنه جعفر بن محمد: تبقية الغنة كالباقين وأطلق الوجهين له صاحب المبهج وكلاهما صحيح

NASHR:v2p25/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r2.speaker: صاحب المبهج
NASHR:v2p25/r2.claim: Al-Muhaj alone omits ghunna before yāʾ for Qunbul through al-Shatwi from Ibn Shanabudh, contrary to the other compilers.
NASHR:v2p25/r2.anchor: وانفرد صاحب المبهج بعدم الغنة عند الياء عن قنبل من طريق الشطوي عن ابن شنبوذ، فخالف سائر المؤلفين

NASHR:v2p25/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p25/r3.claim: The compilers agree on clear pronunciation of silent nūn before wāw or yāʾ inside one word, avoiding confusion with a doubled consonant.
NASHR:v2p25/r3.anchor: وأجمعوا على إظهار النون الساكنة عند الواو والياء إذا اجتمعا في كلمة واحدة نحو صنوان، وقنوان، والدنيا، وبنيان

NASHR:v2p25/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p25/r4.claim: Arabic also preserves nūn before mīm inside a word, as in the cited sheep and goat terms; the Quran has no such example.
NASHR:v2p25/r4.anchor: وكذلك أظهرها العرب مع الميم في الكلمة في نحو قولهم شاة زنماء، وغنم زنم، ولم يقع مثله في القرآن

NASHR:v2p25/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v2p25/r5.claim: Al-Dani excludes nūn from the listed assimilation letters because a silent nūn meeting another nūn must assimilate; the author flags a problem in this account.
NASHR:v2p25/r5.anchor: فكان الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني ممن يذهب إلى عدم ذكرها معهن قال في جامعه

NASHR:v2p25/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p25/r6.claim: The author distinguishes assimilation into unlike letters, where nūn need not be listed, from assimilation generally, where it must; al-Dani follows the latter in al-Taysir.
NASHR:v2p25/r6.anchor: والتحقيق في ذلك أن يقال إن أريد بإدغام النون في غير مثلها فإنه لا وجه لذكر النون

NASHR:v2p25/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن بن كيسان النحوي وأبو بكر بن مجاهد المقري
NASHR:v2p25/r7.claim: Ibn Kaysan and Ibn Mujahid hold that the audible ghunna when nūn assimilates into mīm is the ghunna of the assimilated nūn.
NASHR:v2p25/r7.anchor: فذهب إلى الأول أبو الحسن بن كيسان النحوي، وأبو بكر بن مجاهد المقري، وغيرهما

NASHR:v2p25/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p25/r8.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v2p25/r8.claim: The majority attributes that ghunna to the mīm changed by assimilation, the second of the two explanations named in the excerpt.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r5.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r5.claim: The clear proof and good provision in Shuʿayb's reply mean prophethood and wisdom, ultimate signs of perfection and gifts for everlasting life.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r5.anchor: وذكر قدس سره أن المراد بالبينة والرزق الحسن النبوة والحكمة وأن التعبير عنهما بذلك للتنبيه على أنهما مع كونهما بينة رزق حسن

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r6.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r6.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the reply as conceding that Shuʿayb has long been their guide, then asking whether a true prophet and counselor should stop commanding them to abandon idols and sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r6.anchor: من كلامه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كذا قرره العلامة الطيبي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r7.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r7.claim: Shaykh al-Islam supplies an omitted conditional answer asking whether they would still say such things if Shuʿayb truly had proof, prophethood, and wisdom from God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r7.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف يدله عليه فحوى الكلام أي أتقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r8.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī interprets the good provision as lawful wealth granted by God without strenuous effort.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r8.anchor: وفسر القاضي الرزق الحسن بما آتاه الله تعالى من المال الحلال ومعنى كون ذلك منه تعالى أنه من عنده سبحانه وبإعانته بلا كد في تحصيله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r9.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī takes the conditional answer to ask whether, after God's spiritual and material gifts, Shuʿayb could betray revelation or disobey God's commands; it answers their charge that he changed ancestral practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r9.anchor: وقدر جواب الشرط فهل يسع مع هذا الإنعام الجامع للسعادة الروحانية والجسمانية أن أخون في وحيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r10.claim: Some commentators estimate the conditional answer as al-Ṭībī does.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p118/r10.anchor: وقدر بعضهم ما قدره العلامة الطيبي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r2.claim: On that reading, the good provision would be lawful earnings, as reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r2.anchor: ويكون المراد بالرزق الحسن على ذلك ما آتاه الله تعالى من الحلال فقط كما روي عن الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r3.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r3.claim: Shaykh al-Islam argues that if Shuʿayb was God's prophet and had lawful wealth enough to need no one, he could neither disobey God nor comply with the people's misconduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r3.anchor: أخبروني إن كنت نبيا من عند الله تعالى ورزقني مالا حلالا أستغني به عن العالمين أيصح أن أخالف أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r4.claim: Al-Alusi prefers lawful earnings free from shortchanging and fraud as the good provision meant here.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r4.anchor: المناسب للمقام حمل الرزق الحسن على ما آتاه الله تعالى من الحلال الخالي عن التطفيف والبخس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r6.claim: Their real aim was to stop Shuʿayb's preaching so they could keep worshiping idols and shortchanging; he answers that aim by asking whether a true prophet with lawful, sufficient provision should disobey revelation to satisfy them.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r6.anchor: لم يكن لهم مقصود إلا ترك الدعوة وتركهم وما يفعلون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r7.claim: He does not explicitly answer the slur of madness because it is obviously unworthy of reply; instead, he cuts off their hope of silencing him and hints that their own demand is irrational.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r7.anchor: ولم يتعرض عليه السلام صريحا لرد قولهم المتضمن لرميه وحاشاه بالوسوسة والجنون والسفه والغواية إيذانا بأن ذلك مما لا يستحق جوابا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r8.claim: Mentioning provision alongside proof shows that Shuʿayb has both the reason to preach and freedom from the supposed worldly motive that might restrain him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119/r8.anchor: وكأن التعرض لذكر الرزق مع الكون على بينة للإشارة إلى وجود المقتضى وارتفاع ما يظن مانعا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan parses the interrogative clause as the second object of أرأيتم understood as أخبروني; its answer is supplied by the preceding clause, yielding a question about what is permissible if Shuaib has clear proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r1.anchor: على ما قال أبو حيان في مثل هذا الكلام أعني

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r2.claim: Shuaib says he does not forbid their fraud and then secretly commit it himself by taking for himself what they have abandoned.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r2.anchor: وما أريد ( بنهيي إياكم عما أنهاكم عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r3.claim: In Arabic, خالفني إلى something means he pursued it while I turned away; خالفني عنه reverses the direction, with the speaker pursuing while the other turns away.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r3.anchor: خالفني فلان إلى كذا إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه وخالفني عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr takes أن أخالفكم as the object of أريد, treats خالف as خلف, and reads إلى as attached to أخالف or to an implied مائلا; the sense is that Shuaib will not take their place in doing the forbidden act.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r4.anchor: قال في البحر : والظاهر ما ذكروه أن ( أن أخالفكم ) في موضع المفعول به لأريد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r5.claim: An alternative supplies a coordinated omitted verb, وأميل, before the phrase about turning toward what Shuaib forbids.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : في الكلام فعل محذوف معطوف على المذكور أي وأميل إلى إلخ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r6.claim: Another parsing keeps أخالف in its ordinary sense of opposing: the أن-clause is the object of أريد and إلى attaches to an implied مائلا, or the clause gives the purpose of أريد.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يبقى أخالف على ظاهره من المخالفة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as saying that Shuaib does not intend, by opposing them, to commit what he forbids them.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج في معنى ذلك : أي ما أقصد بخلافكم إلى ارتكاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r8.claim: Shuaib means that everything he says aims only to reform his people through counsel and exhortation, for as long as he is able and without sparing effort.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r8.anchor: بالنصيحة والموعظة ما استطعت أي مدة استطاعتي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r9.claim: Al-Alūsī prefers taking ما as a temporal verbal noun: Shuaib seeks reform throughout the period he remains able to do so.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r10.claim: Another parse makes ما a relative pronoun in apposition to الإصلاح, meaning the amount of reform Shuaib can manage; the apposition may be partitive, complete, or inclusive, with an understood pronoun where required.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r10.anchor: وجوز فيها أن تكون موصولة بدلا من الإصلاح أي المقدار الذي إستطعته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r11.claim: A further parse treats ما استطعت as the direct object of the verbal noun الإصلاح, meaning the corrupt condition of the people that Shuaib can repair.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r11.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن تكون مفعولا به للمصدر المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r12.claim: Al-Alūsī finds the preferred temporal reading stronger: the alternatives add ellipsis and lose emphasis; making the definite verbal noun govern an object is disallowed by Kufans and rare for Basrans, and also leaves an object of استطعت implicit.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r12.anchor: الأبلغ الأظهر ما قدمناه لأن في احتمال البدلية إضمار وفوات المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r13.claim: Shuaib's success in achieving the reform he seeks comes only through God's support and help.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p119#2/r13.anchor: أي ما كوني موفقا لتحقيق ما أتوخاه من إصلاحكم إلا بالله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r1.claim: Some interpret Shuaib's success as guidance to truth and right judgment in everything he does or leaves undone, granted only by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r1.anchor: واختار بعضهم أن يكون المراد وما توفيقي لإصابة الحق والصواب في كل ما آتي وأذر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r2.claim: The apparent sense covers every individual instance of Shuaib's success, since an annexed verbal noun can be generic; alternatively, the whole genus is exclusive, entailing every instance by implication rather than explicitly.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد وما كل فرد من أفراد توفيقي لما صرحوا به من أن المصدر المضاف من صيغ العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r3.speaker: كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r3.claim: Many grammarians supply an omitted genitive after the preposition, yielding the idiomatic sense من عند الله; this avoids linking an agent's action to باء, which grammarians find inelegant because it marks an instrument.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r3.anchor: وتقدير المضاف بعد الباء مما التزمه كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r4.claim: The implied genitive can also clarify that human action is enabled by God's indication and help: indication alone does not produce success without divine aid.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r4.anchor: ومجرد الدلالة لا يجدي بدون المعونة منه عز شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r5.claim: Shuaib relies on God in this matter or all his affairs, since God alone has power while all else is inherently helpless and without standing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p120/r5.anchor: في ذلك أو في جميع أموري لا على غيره فإنه سبحانه القادر المتمكن من كل شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r1.claim: Shuaib returns to God in the matter at hand and directs all his concerns to Him rather than anyone else.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r1.anchor: أي أرجع فيما أنا بصدده أو أقبل بشراشري في مجامع أموري

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r2.claim: The clause is coordinated with what precedes; its present tense, like توكلت, evokes the scene and indicates continuing action despite a past form being more natural for settled realization.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r2.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على ما قبلها وكأن إيثار صيغة الاستقبال فيها على الماضي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r3.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī reads Shuaib's three replies as honoring God's right through gratitude and service, the self's right by restraint, and people's right through reform and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r3.anchor: وفي أنوار التنزيل لأجوبته عليه السلام الثلاثة يعني

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r4.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r4.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī explains the lack of conjunction before إن أريد as confirmation of the preceding answer: someone seeking to take what he forbids for himself would not truly intend reform.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r4.anchor: بما نهى عنه لم يكن مريدا للإصلاح

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r5.claim: The appeal to God's granting success removes any suggestion that Shuaib's mention of ability means he acts independently or arrogantly.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r5.anchor: إزاحة لما عسى أن يوهمه إسناد الاستطاعة إليه بإرادته من استبداده بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r6.claim: The passage points to pure monotheism, as does the pairing of worship and seeking help in the opening of al-Fātiḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r6.anchor: وفيه مع ما بعده إشارة إلى محض التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r7.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r7.claim: Several commentators praise Shuaib's gentle, tactful argument, his effort to win assent and establish truth through seeking divine aid, and his show of having no fear of the unbelievers' hostility.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r7.anchor: مراعاة لطف المراجعة ورفق الاستنزال والمحافظة على حسن المجاراة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r8.claim: Some take Shuaib's return to God as an indirect threat of punishment; the author notes that voluntary turning to God in life is not the same as the compelled return for judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r8.anchor: قيل : وفيه أيضا تهديدهم بالرجوع إلى الله تعالى للجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r9.claim: The author questions the threat reading: in context الإنابة is voluntary turning to God, whereas the return that entails judgment is involuntary.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r9.anchor: أن الإنابة إنما هي الرجوع الاختياري بالفعل إليه سبحانه لا الرجوع الاضطراري للجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r10.claim: Another possible threat is implicit in Shuaib's trust in God, who protects those relying on Him; the text says this need not mean a threat of punishment on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p121/r10.anchor: لكن لا يتعين أن يكون ذلك تهديدا بالجزاء يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r1.speaker: الزجاج واللحياني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Liḥyānī say the word Quran was transferred into a personal proper name, as al-Shāfiʿī and leading legal theorists also hold; on this account it resists ordinary genus-based definition.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج واللحياني لكنه نقل وجعل علما شخصيا كما ذهب إليه الشافعي ومحققو الأصوليين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r2.claim: One proposed definition calls the Quran speech revealed to establish inimitability by even one sūra; al-Ghazālī defines it as what is transmitted with mass attestation between the covers of the codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r2.anchor: ولعل من عرفه بالكلام المنزل للإعجاز بسورة منه أراد تصوير مفهوم لفظ القرآن وكذا من قال كالغزالي أنه ما نقل بين دفتي المصحف تواترا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r3.claim: The codex-based definition distinguishes canonical text from recitation abrogated while its ruling remains and from non-mutawātir material, which do not ground recitation or purity rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r3.anchor: ومما لم ينقل كالمنسوخ تلاوته نحو إنا أنزلنا المال لإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وما نقل ولم يتواتر نحو ثلاثة أيام متتابعات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r4.claim: The inimitability definition is circular and insufficient: inimitability is not an evident essential trait known to all, and identifying a sūra as part of the Quran already presupposes knowing the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r4.anchor: أن كونه للإعجاز ليس لازما بينا إذ لا يعرفه إلا الأفراد من العلماء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r5.claim: The codex definition is likewise circular because recognizing the codex depends on knowing the Quran that is written in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r5.anchor: معرفة المصحف موقوفة على معرفة القرآن إذ ليس هو إلا ما كتب فيه القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r6.speaker: ساداتنا الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r6.claim: The Sufis read the Quran as a sign of the divine Essence in which attributes are effaced, the manifestation of oneness revealed to Muhammad so that unity becomes witnessed in the cosmos.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r6.anchor: أن القرآن إشارة إلى الذات التي يضمحل بها جميع الصفات فهي المجلي المسمى بالأحدية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r7.speaker: ساداتنا الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r7.claim: They interpret the Quran’s descent as the complete manifestation of absolute oneness in Muhammad, with nothing withheld, and its description as noble reflects this incomparable generosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p8/r7.anchor: ومعنى هذا الإنزال أن الحقيقة الأحدية المتعالية في ذراها ظهرت فيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بكمالها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r1.claim: Bayyina means insight and clear explanation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r1.anchor: على بينة} بصيرة وبيان، {من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا} حلالا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r2.claim: One explanation is that the good provision was lawful; another says it was abundant, since Shuʿayb was wealthy; a third says it was knowledge and understanding.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r3.claim: Shuʿayb does not intend to forbid something and then do it himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r3.anchor: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} أي: ما أريد أن أنهاكم عن شيء ثم أرتكبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r4.claim: In what he commands and forbids, Shuʿayb wants only as much reform as he can achieve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r4.anchor: إن أريد} ما أريد فيما [آمركم به وأنهاكم عنه] (1) {إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r5.claim: Tawfīq is the facilitation of the path of good and obedience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r6.claim: To rely on God is to depend on Him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r7.claim: Shuʿayb turns to God when calamities befall him; another explanation is that he returns to Him at the resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p196/r7.anchor: {وإليه أنيب} أرجع فيما ينزل بي من النوائب. وقيل: في المعاد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r1.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says the proficient Qur'an reciter is among the noble, righteous scribes, while one who struggles reciting receives two rewards; Baghawī grades it ṣaḥīḥ and gives a wording variant from Hishām al-Dastawāʾī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " مثل الماهر بالقرآن مثل السفرة الكرام البررة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r2.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r2.claim: The Prophet compares the believer who recites Qur'an to a citron, the believer who does not recite to a date, the wicked reciter to a fragrant but tasteless herb, and the wicked non-reciter to a bitter colocynth; Baghawī calls it ṣaḥīḥ and notes al-Bukhārī's transmission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r2.anchor: عن أنس عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: " مثل المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r3.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r3.claim: The Prophet tells the Qur'an's companion to recite, ascend, and recite as in worldly life; the person's station is at the last verse recited. Al-Tirmidhī calls the report ṣaḥīḥ ḥasan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " يقال لصاحب القرآن اقرأ: وارتق ورتل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r4.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says Qur'an will intercede for its companions; al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān will appear like clouds, canopies, or flocks of birds arguing for their reader, and al-Baqara's recitation is blessing while abandoning it is regret and sorcerers cannot withstand it. Baghawī grades it ṣaḥīḥ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p41#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أنه حدثه قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " اقرؤوا القرآن فإنه يأتي يوم القيامة شافعا لأصحابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r1.claim: The clear proof alludes to the knowledge and prophethood God granted Shuʿayb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله من العلم والنبوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r2.claim: The good provision alludes to lawful wealth given by God, through His help rather than Shuʿayb's own toil.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله من المال الحلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r3.claim: The omitted conditional answer asks whether he could betray revelation and oppose God's command after such spiritual and bodily favors; it answers objections to changing customs and forbidding ancestral religion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r3.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف تقديره فهل يسع مع هذا الإنعام الجامع للسعادات الروحانية والجسمانية

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r4.claim: He does not intend to do what he forbids in order to reserve it for himself; if it were right, he would choose it. The idiom distinguishes going toward what another leaves from going away from it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r4.anchor: لأستبد به دونكم، فلو كان صوابا

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r5.claim: He wants only to reform his people through commanding right and forbidding wrong as far as he can; if their way were sound, he would not forbid it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r5.anchor: أن أصلحكم بأمري بالمعروف ونهيي عن المنكر ما دمت أستطيع الإصلاح

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r6.claim: The three replies are ordered by the three rights a rational person should observe: God's right first, then the self's, then other people's; each requires his commands and prohibitions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r6.anchor: التنبيه على أن العاقل يجب أن يراعي في كل ما يأتيه ويذره

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r7.claim: ما may be a verbal noun functioning as a time adverb, a relative pronoun apposed to الإصلاح meaning the amount he can manage, or part of an elided construction meaning reform of what he can manage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r7.anchor: و { ما } مصدرية واقعة موقع الظرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r8.claim: His ability to attain what is true and right comes only through God's guidance and aid.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r8.anchor: وما توفيقي لإصابة الحق والصواب إلا بهدايته ومعونته

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r9.claim: Exclusive reliance on God expresses pure monotheism: He alone has power, while everything else is inherently helpless; this is the highest knowledge of the Originator.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r9.anchor: فإنه القادر المتمكن من كل شيء وما عداه عاجز في حد ذاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r10.claim: Turning back to God signifies knowledge of the return to Him, and fronting the prepositional phrase gives the expression an exclusive force.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r10.anchor: إشارة إلى معرفة المعاد، وهو أيضا

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r11.claim: These words ask God for right judgment and aid in every affair, declare complete turning to Him, end the unbelievers' hopes, show indifference to their hostility, and warn of return to God for judgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:88/r11.anchor: طلب التوفيق لإصابة الحق فيما يأتيه ويذره من الله تعالى

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r1.claim: The admission that tafsīr is an underdeveloped Arabic discipline gives the author grounds to enter the field within the limits of her ability and expertise.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r1.anchor: من علوم العربية التي لم تنضج ولم تحترق

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r2.claim: She rejects interpretations and approaches she judges distant from authentic Arabic and at odds with the Qur’an’s explicit wording and spirit.

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r3.claim: The Qur’an can unite Arabs across environments, dialects, and cultural inheritances, and unite Muslims across countries and languages in belief, law, and way of life.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r3.anchor: نلوذ بكتابنا الأكبر الذي نلتقي عنده لساناً ووجداناً على اختلاف بيئاتنا ولهجاتنا وتباين ميراثنا الحضاري والفني

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r4.claim: Such unity requires renewed, precise study that penetrates sectarian and doctrinal interpretations and foreign aesthetic tastes to reach the Qur’an’s original core.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r4.anchor: لن يكون هذا التلاقي عند كتابنا العربي المبين

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r5.claim: The book is an attempt to understand the Qur’anic text through Arabic sensibility, attending to every word, vowel, and tone and using the Qur’an itself to resolve disagreement.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r5.anchor: على أن أخلص لفهم النص القرآني

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r6.claim: Her method tracks the Qur’an’s vocabulary and contextual indications, listening closely to the expressive suggestion of its inimitable discourse.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r6.anchor: على هدى التتبع الدقيق لمعجم ألفاظه

BINTSHATI:v1p17/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r7.claim: The method studies one topic across the whole Qur’an, collecting its instances and learning its normal words and patterns, instead of isolating a word or verse in a sūra-by-sūra reading.
BINTSHATI:v1p17/r7.anchor: التناول الموضوعي الذي يفرغ لدراسة الموضوع الواحد فيه، فيجمع كل ما في القرآن منه، ويهتدى بمألوف استعماله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r4.claim: Shuʿayb appeals to their kinship and asks them to think fairly through a hypothetical case to encourage agreement and impartiality.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r4.anchor: مستعطفا لهم بما بينهم من عواطف القرابة منبها لهم على حسن النظر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r6.claim: Bayyinah means proof, and the hypothetical wording presents Shuʿayb as firmly established upon proof from his Lord.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r7.claim: Shuʿayb says God granted him abundant, lawful wealth in which he wronged no one.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r7.anchor: جليلا ومالا جما حلالا لم أظلم فيه أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r8.claim: The answer to the hypothetical is omitted so the audience can consider every implication, including whether justice makes Shuʿayb foolish or allows him to abandon God's call.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r8.anchor: والجواب مجذوف لتذهب النفس فيه كل مذهب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r9.claim: Shuʿayb denies ever doing what he forbids, and says that leaving their fraud is guidance rather than wasteful opposition.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r9.anchor: ما فعلت قط ما نهيتكم عنه فيما مضى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r10.claim: Biqaʿi illustrates the point with a maxim against forbidding a vice while committing it oneself.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r10.anchor: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي بمثله عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r11.claim: Shuʿayb’s sole aim is reform to the limit of his capacity; his just financial conduct demonstrates that fairness is not wasteful.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r11.anchor: أي ما { أريد } أي شيئا من الأشياء { إلا الإصلاح }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r12.claim: His reasoning honors three rights in all conduct: God’s first, the self’s second, and other people’s third, with sincerity in each.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r12.anchor: أن العقل يجب أن يراعي في كل ما يأتي ويذر أحد حقوق ثلاثه أهمها وأعلاها حق الله وثانيها حق النفس وثالثها حق العباد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r13.claim: Tawfīq is the creation of a capacity that fits an act of obedience, from the idea of matching or agreement.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r13.anchor: والوفيق : خلق قدرة ما هو وفق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r14.claim: Shuʿayb attributes success in reform to God alone and disclaims independent power or strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r14.anchor: ثم تبرأ من الحول والقوة , وأسند الأمر إلى من هو له

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r15.claim: Reliance on God entrusts affairs to Him, accepts His management, and remains committed to obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r15.anchor: تفويض الأمر إليه على الرضاء بتدبيره مع التمسك بطاعته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r16.claim: Shuʿayb turns wholly to God, renewing repentance because of the magnitude of the task; the wording also warns of resurrection and strengthens belief in return after death.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p567/r16.anchor: يجدد التوبة لعظم الأمرن وعبر عن ذلك بعبارة

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the good provision as lawful.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا} قال: الحلال

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r5.claim: Qatada says Shuʿayb does not forbid something and then do it himself.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} يقول: لم أك لأنهاكم عن أمر واركبه

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r6.claim: When challenged about hair extensions, Ibn Masʿud invoked the righteous servant’s commitment not to act against his own prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r6.anchor: عن مسروق رضي الله عنه أن امرأة جاءت إلى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه فقالت: اتنهى عن المواصلة قال: نعم

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r7.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r7.claim: Muʿawiya al-Qushayri’s brother accuses Muhammad of doing the opposite of his orders; the Prophet says any such fault would be his own.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r7.anchor: عن معاوية القشيري أن أخاه مالكا قال: يا معاوية إن محمدا أخذ جيراني فانطلق إليه

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r8.speaker: مالك بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r8.claim: Malik ibn Dinar describes the truthful admonisher being crowned and admitted to Paradise, with his supporters receiving the same honor.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r8.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ هذه الآية {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} قال: بلغني أنه يدعى يوم القيامة بالمذكر الصادق

DURR-FULL:v4p467/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r9.speaker: أبو إسحق الفزاري
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari says reciting this verse when weighing an action strengthened his resolve toward right guidance.
DURR-FULL:v4p467/r9.anchor: عن أبي إسحق الفزاري رضي الله عنه قال: ما أردت أمرا قط فتلوت عنده هذه الآية إلا عزم لي على الرشد

DURR-FULL:v4p468/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses «to Him I turn» as «to Him I return».
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وإليه أنيب} قال: إليه أرجع

DURR-FULL:v4p468/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r2.claim: Ali asks the Prophet for counsel; he says to affirm God as Lord and remain steadfast, then praises Ali’s deep learning. The chain contains Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kuraymi.
DURR-FULL:v4p468/r2.anchor: عن علي قال: قلت: يا رسول الله أوصني قال قل ربي الله ثم استقم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r1.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r1.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni glosses being upon clear proof from his Lord as being certain.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا عمران الجوني قرا هذه الاية : اني على بينة من ربي قال : على ثقة

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains good provision as lawful provision.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك رزقا حسنا قال : الرزق الحسن : الحلال

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r3.speaker: مسروق
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r3.claim: Masruq reports that Ibn Masud forbade hair extensions and, when challenged about his household, answered by invoking Shuayb's pledge not to practice what he forbids.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r3.anchor: عن مسروق ان امراة جاءت ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه فقالت اتنهى عن الواصلة قال : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r4.claim: Qatada explains that Shuayb would not forbid an act and then commit it himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وما اريد ان اخالفكم إلى ماانهاكم عنه يقول لم اكن انهاكم عن امر واركبه

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r5.speaker: أبو سليمان الضبي
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r5.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dabbi says Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's letters to Khurasan gave commands and prohibitions and closed by citing that success comes only from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r5.anchor: عن أبي سليمان الضبي قال : كانت تجيئنا كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز إلى خراسان فيها الامر والنهي فيكتب في اخرها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses returning to God as returning to Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : واليه انيب قال : اليه ارجع

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r7.speaker: عبيد بن يعلى
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Yala says turning back to God means supplication.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2073/r7.anchor: عن عبيد بن يعلى قال : الانابه : الدعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr notes that this statement parallels the corresponding passages in Noah’s and Ṣāliḥ’s stories.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r1.anchor: تقدم نظير الآية في قصة نوح وقصة صالح عليهما السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r2.claim: The good provision is prophethood, called provision by analogy with Noah’s and Ṣāliḥ’s mention of mercy and in verbal accommodation to the people’s mention of wealth in 11:87.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالرزق الحسن هنا مثل المراد من الرحمة في كلام نوح وكلام صالح عليهما السلام وهو نعمة النبوءة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r3.claim: The conditional’s answer is omitted, supplied by context: what could justify denying him or save them from its consequences? The hypothetical warning urges them to consider his truth or examine the prohibition’s benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r3.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف يدل عليه سياق الكلام ، أو يدل عليه { إن كنت على بينة من ربي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r4.speaker: جميع المفسرين من التابعين فمن بعدهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r4.claim: Commentators from the Successors onward understand Shُayb to deny forbidding people something while secretly doing it himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r4.anchor: ومعنى { وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه } عند جميع المفسرين من التابعين فمن بعدهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r5.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r5.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains the idiom as someone pursuing something while the other person turns away from it, illustrated by one traveler going toward water as another leaves it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r5.anchor: وبين في ( الكشاف ) إفادة التركيب هذا المعنى بقوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r6.claim: The construction makes مخالفة imply adopting the opposite state; إلى marks the endpoint of the pursuit, أخالفكم is understood as seeking, and أن أخالفكم is the object of أريد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r6.anchor: وبيانه أن المخالفة تدل على الاتصاف بضد حاله ، فإذا ذكرت في غرض دلت على الاتصاف بضده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r7.claim: On the reported reading, he would turn them away from forbidden acts while himself turning toward those same acts; he denies that hypocritical conduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r7.anchor: أي أن أفعل خلاف الأفعال التي نهيتكم عنها بأن أصرفكم عنها وأنا أصير إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r8.claim: A legal address to the community includes the Messenger unless evidence singles him out, so what he forbids them is forbidden to him as well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r8.anchor: كما قال علماؤنا : إن خطاب الأمة يشمل الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ما لم يدل دليل على تخصيصه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r9.claim: The prohibition is for their benefit and distinguishes Shُayb from rulers who forbid acts they themselves perform; that hypocrisy signals lack of sincere counsel, as reproved in 2:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r9.anchor: وفي هذا تنبيه لهم على ما في النهي من المصلحة ، وعلى أن شأنه ليس شأن الجبابرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r10.claim: He connects the reproach of forbidding others while neglecting oneself to the Qur’anic rebuke in 2:44 about commanding righteousness and forgetting oneself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p143#3/r10.anchor: أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers مخالفة as opposition or contention: Shُayb may have sensed that they suspected him of seeking domination, or he sought to dispel hostile thoughts before they arose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r1.anchor: والذي يظهر لي في معنى الآية أن المراد من المخالفة المعاكسة والمنازعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r2.claim: This broader reading answers their charge in 11:87: Shُayb denies mere contrarianism and says his opposition serves the higher purpose of reform, rather than merely faulting them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r2.anchor: فإنهم ظنوا به أنه ما قصد إلا مخالفتهم وتخطئتهم ونفوا أن يكون له قصد صالح فيما دعاهم إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وعمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r3.claim: A report about the Fazāra delegation has Abū Bakr and ʿUmar exchange the phrase about not intending to oppose one another, illustrating this idiom; no grading is given.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق : ( أمر الأقرع بن حابس ، وقال عمر : أمر فلانا ، فقال أبو بكر لعمر : ما أردت إلى خلافي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
