IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r4.claim: He distinguishes critics who stop at finding fault from those who identify an error and then explain how to correct it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r4.anchor: قسم ينتقد الشيء ويقف عند حد النقد دون ارتقاء إلى بيان ما يصلح المنقود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r5.claim: On his preferred parsing, إلى ما أنهاكم and أن أخالفكم both depend on أريد, with a deleted preposition before the latter: he does not want prohibition for the sake of opposing them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه يتعلق { إلى ما أنهاكم } بفعل { أريد } وكذلك { أن أخالفكم } يتعلق ب { أريد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r6.claim: The reform clause explains the preceding denial: the positive aim is reform for as long as he can achieve it, expressed as a reversal restriction (qaṣr qalb).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r6.anchor: فبينه بأن الضد المراد إثباته هو الإصلاح في جميع أوقات استطاعته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p144/r7.claim: The restriction reverses the audience’s assumption: opposition is not the aim; reform is. Its force comes from affirming the opposite of what they suspected.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r1.claim: The restrictive form intensifies the assertion beyond simple negation and affirmation; Ibn ʿĀshūr illustrates the contrastive form with a line attributed either to ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Ḥārithī or al-Samawʾal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r1.anchor: كقول عبد الملك بن عبد الرحيم الحارثي أو السموءل : تسيل على حد الظبات نفوسنا وليست على غير الظبات تسيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r2.claim: After explaining an action that could invite self-praise, Shُayb attributes its success to God: reform is divine enabling, occurring only by God’s will and guidance; the clause is circumstantial to أريد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r2.anchor: ولما بين لهم حقيقة عمله وكان في بيانه ما يجر الثناء على نفسه أعقبه بإرجاع الفضل في ذلك إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r3.claim: Tawfīq literally makes one thing accord with another; theologians define it as creating the capacity and motivation to obey.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r3.anchor: والتوفيق : جعل الشيء وفقا لآخر ، أي طبقا له ، ولذلك عرفوه بأنه خلق القدرة والداعية إلى الطاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r4.claim: عليه توكلت is circumstantial either of the divine name or of the first-person suffix in توفيقي, since a genitive noun can be treated as part of its governing noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r4.anchor: وجملة { عليه توكلت } في موضع الحال من اسم الجلالة ، أو من ياء المتكلم في قوله : { توفيقي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr points back to his discussion of reliance on God at 3:159.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r5.anchor: والتوكل مضى عند قوله تعالى : { فإذا عزمت فتوكل على الله } في سورة آل عمران ( 159 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r6.claim: He points back to the earlier explanation of ināba in the description of Abraham at 11:75.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p145/r6.anchor: والإنابة تقدمت آنفا في قوله : { إن إبراهيم لحليم أواه منيب } ( هود : 75 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r1.claim: The order of verses was fixed by the Prophet under revelation brought by Gabriel, who recited each newly revealed verse in its designated place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r1.anchor: فكانت وحيا نزل به جبريل ، فقرئ مع الآية التي نزل بأثرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r2.claim: The mosquito parable in al-Baqara follows the promise of the Garden because it answers polytheists who objected that Muhammad should not give examples of a fly or spider, then moves from one parable to their objection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r2.anchor: كان ردا على المشركين في قولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r3.claim: Verse placement may have an apparent connection, but sometimes its occasion explains its position even when the surrounding topic seems unrelated, as with the passage about revelation in al-Qiyama.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r3.anchor: وقد لا تكون له مناسبة ولكنه اقتضاه سبب في ذلك المكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r4.claim: Al-Bukhari reports Ibn Abbas saying that when Gabriel brought revelation, the Prophet moved his tongue and lips to memorize it, prompting the passage in al-Qiyama.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r4.anchor: روى البخاري عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله إذا نزل جبريل بالوحي كان مما يحرك به لسانه وشفتيه يريد أن يحفظه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r5.claim: A verse may follow the last verse revealed during the sura’s revelation period because its occasion occurred then, even if the thematic link is not apparent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r5.anchor: قد يكون سبب وضعها في موضعها أنها قد نزلت على سبب وكان حدوث سبب نزولها في مدة نزول السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r6.claim: The command to guard the prayers was placed amid many rules about spouses and mothers, and Ibn Ashur says he discussed its occasion at that verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r6.anchor: بين تشريعات أحكام كثيرة في شؤون الأزواج والأمهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Ibn Abbas’s report that the command to fear the Day of Return was appended after the sura’s completion by an instruction to place it after a specified verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في آية ) واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r8.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Ibn Masud reports that the opening of al-Hadid was revealed in Mecca, while its passage beginning with the call to spend was revealed in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r8.anchor: ما روى في صحيح مسلم عن ابن مسعود أن أول سورة الحديد نزل بمكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r9.claim: The late Medinan passage in al-Hadid fits the sura through thematic relation and similarity of style; its delayed revelation was likely tied to a later occasion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r9.anchor: فلا يكون ذلك إلا لمناسبة بينها وبين آي تلك السورة والتشابه في أسلوب النظم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r10.claim: Because reports fixing verse placement are few, an exegete should seek a plausible relation wherever possible and otherwise avoid forced explanations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r10.anchor: كان حقا على المفسر أن يتطلب مناسبات لمواقع الآيات ما وجد إلى ذلك سبيلا موصلا وإلا فليعرض عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r11.claim: The Qur’an’s main purpose is reforming the whole community: calling unbelievers to faith and sound worship, and guiding believers’ morals, steadfastness, success, and purification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r11.anchor: إن الغرض الأكبر للقرآن هو إصلاح الأمة بأسرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r12.claim: Because each verse serves reform, proof, guidance, or correction, the Qur’an need not proceed as a continuous treatise; like a preacher, it shifts among current concerns and inserts instructive parenthetical statements.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r12.anchor: لأن كل آية منه ترجع إلى غرض الإصلاح والاستدلال عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r13.claim: In the cited passage about a faction of the People of the Book, the sentence declaring that guidance is God’s guidance is parenthetical.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p80/r13.anchor: إن الهدى هدى الله ( جملة معترضة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r1.claim: Shuayb’s reply is a gentle, skillful appeal that draws his audience toward the truth; the Prophet called him the orator of the prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r1.anchor: هذه مراجعة لطيفة واستنزال حسن واستدعاء رفيق ونحوها عن محاورة شعيب عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r2.claim: The Prophet described Shuayb as the orator of the prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r2.anchor: قال فيه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ذاك خطيب الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r3.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer, approximately: ‘Should I go astray like you and abandon conveying the message?’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r3.anchor: وجواب الشرط الذي في قوله: إن كنت على بينة من ربي محذوف تقديره: أأضل كما ضللتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r4.claim: Bayyina may mean clarification or proof, with its feminine ending marking intensity, or it may be a feminine adjective modifying an omitted noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r4.anchor: وبينة يحتمل أن تكون بمعنى: بيان أو بين، ودخلت الهاء للمبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r5.claim: The good provision Shuayb received is pure wealth, free of the corruption the people introduced into their earnings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r5.anchor: ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا يريد: خالصا من الفساد الذي أدخلتم أنتم أموالكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r6.claim: Shuayb says he will not commit the fraud he forbids—shorting measures and weights—to enrich himself; he seeks reform for everyone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r6.anchor: ولست أريد أن أفعل الشيء الذي نهيتكم عنه من نقص الكيل والوزن، فأستأثر بالمال لنفسي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p201/r7.claim: Anibu means that Shuayb returns, repents, and relies on God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī refers this phrase to his earlier explanations at Hūd 28 and 63.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r1.anchor: ( إن كنت على بينة من ربي ) قد تقدم تفسيره [ هود 28 و 63 ]

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the good provision is lawful wealth and adds that Shuʿayb was wealthy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه الحلال قال ابن عباس وكان شعيب كثير المال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r3.claim: A second interpretation identifies the good provision as prophethood.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r4.claim: A third interpretation identifies it as knowledge and understanding.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the conditional's answer is omitted: if Shuʿayb had proof from God, would he follow error? The audience can supply the meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج وجواب الشرط هاهنا متروك والمعنى إن كنت على بينة من ربي أتبع الضلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r6.claim: Qatāda explains that Shuʿayb would not forbid an act and then commit it himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r6.anchor: قال قتادة لم أكن لأنهاكم عن أمر ثم أرتكبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says Shuʿayb does not intend, by opposing them, to pursue the very act he forbids.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج ما أقصد بخلافكم القصد إلى ارتكابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r8.claim: He seeks only to set their affairs right as far as he can; his capacity is to deliver the message, not to compel them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p150/r8.anchor: أي ما أريد بما آمركم به إلا إصلاح أموركم بقدر طاقتي وقدر طاقتي إبلاغكم لا إجباركم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r1.claim: The Medinan readers and Ibn ʿĀmir pronounce the tāʾ in tawfīqī with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r1.anchor: فتح تاء توفيقي أهل المدينة وابن عامر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r2.claim: Shuʿayb's success in reaching the truth while trying to reform his people comes only from God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r2.anchor: ومعنى الكلام ما أصابتي الحق في محاولة صلاحكم إلى بالله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r3.claim: He has entrusted his affair to God because his people threatened to expel him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p151/r3.anchor: أي فوضت أمري وذلك أنهم تواعدوه بقولهم ( لنخرجنك يا شعيب ) [ الأعراف 88 ]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r1.claim: Shuayb asks whether they see that he has clear insight from his Lord about what he calls them to.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r1.anchor: إن كنت على بينة من ربي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r2.claim: One reported explanation takes the good provision as prophethood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r2.anchor: قيل: أراد النبوة. وقيل: أراد الرزق الحلال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r3.claim: Another reported explanation takes the good provision as lawful livelihood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r3.anchor: قيل: أراد النبوة. وقيل: أراد الرزق الحلال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r4.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r4.claim: Al-Thawri explains that Shuayb does not secretly do what he forbids them, acting differently out of their sight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r4.anchor: وقال الثوري: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} أي: لا أنهاكم عن شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r5.claim: Qatada explains that Shuayb would not forbid an act and then commit it himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r5.anchor: كما قال قتادة في قوله: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه} يقول: لم أكن لأنهاكم عن أمر وأركبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r6.claim: His only aim in commanding and forbidding is to reform them to the extent of his effort and ability.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r7.claim: Tawfiq means success in attaining the truth in what he seeks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r7.anchor: وما توفيقي} أي: في إصابة الحق فيما أريده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r8.claim: Shuayb entrusts all his affairs to God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r9.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r9.claim: Aniba means that Shuayb returns to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r9.anchor: وإليه أنيب} أي: أرجع، قاله مجاهد وغيره.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r10.speaker: معاوية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r10.claim: In Ahmad’s report, Malik asks his brother Muawiya to appeal to Muhammad to release their Muslim neighbors; when challenged that he might forbid and secretly do otherwise, the Prophet says any such blame would fall on him alone and releases them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r10.anchor: عن حكيم بن معاوية، عن أبيه: أن أخاه مالكا قال: يا معاوية، إن محمدا أخذ جيراني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r11.speaker: جد بهز بن حكيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r11.claim: A second report says the Prophet detained some of the narrator’s people on suspicion; when confronted with the charge of forbidding what he privately does, he says the blame would be his and orders the neighbors released.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p344/r11.anchor: عن بهز (7) بن حكيم، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: أخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ناسا من قومي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r1.claim: The Prophet says reports recognized by the heart and welcomed by the body as familiar are most truly his, while reports the heart and body reject are farthest from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r1.anchor: عن عبد الملك بن سعيد بن سويد الأنصاري قال: سمعت أبا حميد وأبا أسيد يقولان: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this chain sound and notes that Muslim transmits another hadith through it about supplications when entering and leaving a mosque.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r2.anchor: إسناد صحيح، وقد أخرج مسلم بهذا السند حديث:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r3.claim: The hadith means that any good reported from the Prophet is most truly his, while any bad report is furthest from him, in keeping with the pledge not to act contrary to one’s prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r3.anchor: ومعناه -والله أعلم -: مهما بلغكم عني من خير فأنا أولاكم به ومهما يكن من مكروه فأنا أبعدكم منه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r4.claim: A woman asks Ibn Masud whether he forbids hair extensions and whether one of his wives might wear them; he invokes the righteous servant’s pledge not to act contrary to his prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r4.anchor: عن مسروق، أن امرأة جاءت ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r5.speaker: العتبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r5.claim: Al-Utbi says Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ended letters of command and prohibition by echoing Shuayb’s words of reliance and return to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p345/r5.anchor: وقال عثمان بن أبي شيبة: حدثنا جرير، عن أبي سليمان العتبي (10) قال: كانت تجيئنا كتب عمر بن عبد العزيز

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report disconnected because al-Hasan did not meet Umar; he understands it to mean Umar initiated collection and supervised its preservation and compilation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r1.anchor: هذا منقطع، فإن الحسن لم يدرك عمر، ومعناه: أشار بجمعه فجمع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r2.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r2.claim: Yahya reports that Umar would accept no Qur'anic material for the collection without two witnesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب، أن عمر لما جمع القرآن كان لا يقبل من أحد شيئا حتى يشهد شاهدان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r3.speaker: عروة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r3.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr feared the Qur'an would be lost after many reciters were killed and ordered Umar and Zayd to write any material supported by two witnesses; Ibn Kathir grades the disconnected report fair.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: لما استحر القتل بالقراء يومئذ فرق أبو بكر، رضي الله عنه، أن يضيع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r4.claim: Zayd says he found the ending of Surat al-Tawba with Abu Khuzayma al-Ansari, also identified in a report as Khuzayma b. Thabit, and no one else; they wrote it because the Prophet had counted Khuzayma's testimony as two.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r4.anchor: ولهذا قال زيد بن ثابت: وجدت آخر سورة التوبة، يعني قوله تعالى: {لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r5.speaker: خزيمة بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r5.claim: Khuzayma's testimony was counted as two after he affirmed the Prophet's purchase of a horse when its Bedouin seller denied the sale.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r5.anchor: وفي رواية: مع خزيمة بن ثابت الذي جعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شهادته بشهادتين لم أجدها مع غيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r6.claim: Abu al-Aliyah reports that Ubayy b. Ka'b dictated the two verses to the collectors together with Khuzayma b. Thabit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r6.anchor: عن الربيع عن أبي العالية أن أبي بن كعب أملاها عليهم مع خزيمة بن ثابت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r7.speaker: يحيى بن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r7.claim: Yahya also reports that Uthman testified to the same material found for the collection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r7.anchor: عن يحيى ابن عبد الرحمن بن حاطب؛ أن عثمان شهد بذلك أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r8.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r8.claim: Zayd describes gathering the Qur'an from palm stalks, flat stones, and the memories of men; another wording lists sheets, shoulder blades, and camel gear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p26/r8.anchor: وأما قول زيد [بن ثابت] (2) "فتتبعت القرآن أجمعه من العسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r1.claim: Uthman explains that the Prophet placed revealed verses in designated surahs; Anfal came early in Medina and Bara'a late, their stories were similar, and the Prophet died without clarifying whether Bara'a belonged with Anfal, so Uthman joined them without basmala among the seven long surahs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r1.anchor: وكانت الأنفال من أول ما نزل بالمدينة، وكانت براءة من آخر القرآن، وكانت قصتها شبيهة بقصتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that the order of verses and surahs was transmitted from the Prophet, while the arrangement of surahs in the codex was Uthman's work; reciting in reverse order is a serious error.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r2.anchor: ففهم من هذا الحديث أن ترتيب الآيات والسور أمر توقيفي متلقى عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأما ترتيب السور فمن أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r3.claim: Following Uthman's surah sequence is recommended; continuous recitation as the Prophet did is preferable, though separating surahs is permitted, as shown by his Friday and Eid recitations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p29/r3.anchor: وأما ترتيب السور فمستحب اقتداء بعثمان، رضي الله عنه، والأولى إذا قرأ أن يقرأ متواليا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that the material people call al-Mufassal is al-Muhkam, and that he had read it by the Prophet's death at age ten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا ابن عشر سنين وقد قرأت المحكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports collecting al-Muhkam during the Prophet's lifetime and identifies al-Muhkam as al-Mufassal; al-Bukhari alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: جمعت المحكم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت له: وما المحكم؟ قال: "المفصل"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the report as evidence that teaching children Qur'an is permissible, and says it may even be recommended or obligatory: early learning equips a child to pray and makes memorization more lasting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r3.anchor: وفيه دلالة على جواز تعلم الصبيان القرآن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r4.claim: A Bukhari report says Ibn Abbas was circumcised when the Prophet died; since boys were circumcised at puberty, Ibn Kathir allows that he rounded his age down to ten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r4.anchor: وقد روى البخاري أنه قال: توفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا مختون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r5.claim: Some early authorities recommended letting a child play briefly at first, then directing his attention to reading, to avoid making him resent and abandon it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r5.anchor: وقد استحب بعض السلف أن يترك الصبي في ابتداء عمره قليلا للعب، ثم توفر همته على القراءة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r6.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r6.claim: Some scholars disliked teaching Qur'an to a child who cannot understand; they advised waiting until discernment, then teaching gradually according to capacity, interest, memory, and intelligence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r6.anchor: وكره بعضهم تعليمهم القرآن وهو لا يعقل ما يقال له، ولكن يترك حتى إذا عقل وميز علم قليلا قليلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r7.claim: Umar recommended teaching a child five verses at a time; Ibn Kathir says the report has a good chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p74/r7.anchor: واستحب عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، أن يلقن خمس آيات خمس آيات، رويناه عنه بسند جيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r1.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r1.claim: A report from Usayd says he recited Qur'an in a fine voice on his rooftop, then relates an account like the one that follows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r1.anchor: عن ابن كعب بن مالك، عن أسيد بن حضير: أنه كان على ظهر بيته يقرأ القرآن وهو حسن الصوت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r2.speaker: أسيد بن حضير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r2.claim: Usayd says that while he recited at night he heard a thud and saw lamp-like lights filling the space between heaven and earth; the Prophet explained that angels had descended for the recitation, and Usayd could have seen wonders if he continued.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r3.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r3.claim: Al-Bara' reports that a man reciting Surat al-Kahf at night saw a cloud-like form above his running horse; the Prophet said sakina had descended for the Qur'an. Ibn Kathir says this apparently was Usayd and notes the unusual suspended form in Bukhari.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r3.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق سمع البراء يقول: بينما رجل يقرأ سورة الكهف ليلة إذ رأى دابته تركض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says the reports support the chapter's account of sakina and angels descending during Qur'an recitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا هو أسيد بن الحضير، رضي الله عنه، فهذا ما يتعلق بصناعة الإسناد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r5.speaker: أشياخ أهل المدينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r5.claim: Medinan elders reported that Thabit b. Qays's house shone like lamps one night; the Prophet guessed that he had recited al-Baqara, and Thabit confirmed it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p55/r5.anchor: أن أشياخ أهل المدينة حدثوه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قيل له: ألم تر ثابت بن قيس بن شماس لم تزل داره البارحة تزهر مصابيح

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r3.claim: Tawfiq is agreement with what is right, not a distinct kind of thing but whatever is known to lead to right; only God knows what does so, making Him the sole source of guidance and aid.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r3.anchor: التوفيق: من الموافقة، وهو الاتفاق للصواب هو فعل ما يتفق عنده الصواب، وليس ذلك جنسا بعينه

JISHUMI:v5p3551/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r4.claim: Tawfiq belongs among divine لطف, though the term is reserved for the لطف in which right action actually occurs; it can be a blessing or a trial.
JISHUMI:v5p3551/r4.anchor: ثم يكون نعمة وبلية، والله الموفق للصواب فقط؛ لأنه لم يعلم ما يتفق الصواب عنده إلا الله تعالى

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r1.claim: The conditional has an omitted answer: if Shu'ayb has clear proof and provision from God, he will not leave his worship, which is all the more reason to worship.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r1.anchor: ويقال: أين جواب قوله: (إن كنت على بينة)؟ قلنا: محذوف، وتقديره: إن كنت على بينة من ربي

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r2.claim: Another proposed sense asks what the people should do if they accuse Shu'ayb of falsehood while he has proof, and what excuse they have for refusing faith.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r2.anchor: قيل: أرأيتم إن كذبتموني، وأنا على بينة من ربي، فما تصنعون؟ وما عذركم في ترك الإيمان؟

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r3.claim: A further explanation asks why Shu'ayb would turn away from worship and prayer to God when he has clear proof and provision from Him.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r3.anchor: وقيل: إذا كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقه، فلماذا أعدل عن عبادته والدعاء إليه؟

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r4.claim: Bayyina here means a proof from God, who establishes the evidence.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r4.anchor: بينة حجة من ربي؛ لأنه ينصب الأدلة

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r5.claim: One gloss is good, lawful provision obtained without shortchanging others.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r5.anchor: قيل: حلالا طيبا من غير بخس

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r6.claim: Another gloss takes the provision to mean knowledge and understanding.

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r7.claim: A further gloss identifies the good provision as prophethood and revealed law.

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r8.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r8.claim: The line cited illustrates that Shu'ayb does not forbid a vice and then commit it himself.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r8.anchor: نحو قول الشاعر: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله ... عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r9.claim: Another explanation is that Shu'ayb does not prohibit their fraud in order to gain for himself what they stop doing.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r9.anchor: وقيل: ليس نهيي إياكم لمنفعة أجرها إلى نفسي بما تتركون من التطفيف

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r10.claim: Shu'ayb seeks only to reform people's religious and worldly affairs as far as he can.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r10.anchor: إن أريد إلا الإصلاح أي: لا أريد إلا إصلاح أمور الناس في دينهم ودنياهم ما استطعت

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r11.claim: His actions do not come from his own power or strength, but from God's help, facilitation, and لطف.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r11.anchor: أي: ما أفعله ليس بحولي وقوتي بل بمعونة الله وتيسيره ولطفه

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r12.claim: To rely on God is to entrust one's affair to Him.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r12.anchor: عليه توكلت أي: فوضت أمري إليه

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r13.claim: One explanation is that Shu'ayb returns to God in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r13.anchor: وإليه أنيب قيل: أرجع إليه في المعاد

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r14.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r14.claim: Al-Hasan says Shu'ayb returns to God with his deeds and intentions.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r14.anchor: وقيل: إليه أرجع بعملي ونيتي، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v5p3552/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r15.claim: Another interpretation is that Shu'ayb turns to God in all his affairs.
JISHUMI:v5p3552/r15.anchor: وقيل: أرجع إليه في جميع أموري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r1.claim: منه means from God's presence; the good provision is the prophethood and wisdom granted to Shuʿayb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r1.anchor: ورزقني منه } أي من لدنه { رزقا حسنا } وهو ما رزقه من النبوة والحكمة .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r2.claim: Alternatively, his good provision is lawful, wholesome wealth, untainted by shortchanging or fraud.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r2.anchor: وقيل { رزقا حسنا } حلالا طيبا من غير بخس ولا تطفيف .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r3.claim: The answer to أرأيتم is omitted: the answer was made explicit in the Noah and Lot accounts, and the meaning makes its place clear here.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r3.anchor: جوابه محذوف ، وإنما لم يثبت لأن إثباته في القصتين دل على مكانه ، ومعنى الكلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r4.claim: If Shuʿayb truly has clear proof and is a genuine prophet, he cannot refrain from ordering them to abandon idols and sins, since that is why prophets are sent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r4.anchor: ومعنى الكلام ينادي عليه . والمعنى : أخبروني إن كنت على حجة واضحة ويقين من ربي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r5.claim: To differ toward something is to go to it while the other person turns away; to differ away from it reverses their directions, illustrated by travelers going to and from water.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r5.anchor: يقال : خالفني فلان إلى كذا : إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه ، وخالفني عنه إذا ولي عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r6.claim: Shuʿayb says he does not intend to get ahead of them in forbidden pleasures and reserve them for himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r6.anchor: يعني أن أسبقكم إلى شهواتكم التي نهيتكم عنها ، لأستبد بها دونكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r7.claim: His only aim is to reform them through admonition, counsel, commanding right, and forbidding wrong.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r7.anchor: ما أريد إلا أن أصلحكم بموعظتي ونصيحتي وأمري بالمعروف ونهي عن المنكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r8.claim: ما استطعت may be an adverbial phrase meaning for as long as he can reform and while able, sparing no effort.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r8.anchor: ظرف ، أي : مدة استطاعتي للإصلاح ، وما دمت متمكنا منه لا آلو فيه جهدا .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r9.claim: Alternatively, ما استطعت is an apposition to الإصلاح, specifying the amount of reform he can manage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r9.anchor: أو بدل من الإصلاح ، أي : المقدار الذي استطعته منه .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r10.claim: Alternatively, it means إصلاح ما استطعت with the noun إصلاح omitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على تقدير حذف المضاف على قولك : إلا الإصلاح إصلاح ما استطعت .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r11.claim: Alternatively, it is a purpose object, illustrated by ضعيف النكاية أعداءه; the sense is reforming whatever of their corruption he can.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r11.anchor: أو مفعول له كقوله : ضعيف النكاية أعداءه ; أي ما أريد إلا أن أصلح ما استطعت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r12.claim: Success in attaining truth and acting in accordance with God's pleasure depends entirely on His help and support.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r12.anchor: وما كوني موفقا لإصابة الحق فيما آتي وأذر ، ووقوعه موافقا لرضا الله إلا بمعونته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r13.claim: Shuʿayb asks God to carry the matter through as it should and support him against his enemy, implicitly threatening the unbelievers and ending their hopes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p396/r13.anchor: استوفق ربه في إمضاء الأمر على سننه ، وطلب منه التأييد والإظهار على عدوه ، وفي ضمنه تهديد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the good provision as lawful wealth; Ibn ʿAbbās adds that Shuʿayb was very wealthy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r2.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says the good provision means prophethood.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r3.claim: The wording omits a clause, understood as: would I turn away from worship despite this proof and provision?
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r3.anchor: وفي الكلام محذوف وتقديره , أفأعدل مع ذلك عن عبادته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r4.claim: Shuʿayb will not do what he forbids them, just as he will not abandon what he commands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r4.anchor: أي لا أفعل ما نهيتكم عنه كما لا أترك ما أمرتكم به

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r5.claim: He intends only to act righteously as far as he can; ability conditions action, not intention.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r5.anchor: ما أريد إلا فعل الصلاح ما استطعت , لأن الاستطاعة من شرط الفعل دون الإرادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r6.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r6.claim: Mujāhid takes ināba as returning: “to Him I return.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r6.anchor: أن الإنابة الرجوع ومعناه وإليه أرجع , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r7.speaker: عبيد الله بن يعلى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r7.claim: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Yaʿlā takes ināba as supplication: “to Him I pray.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p497/r7.anchor: أن الإنابة الدعاء , ومعناه وإليه أدعو , عبيد الله بن يعلى

MUJAHID:v1p307#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p307#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p307#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains “to Him I turn” as “I return.”
MUJAHID:v1p307#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وإليه أنيب ﴾ يعني أرجع

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r6.claim: Shuayb's good provision from God means faith, which is guidance.
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r6.anchor: قال يقوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي ورزقني منه رزقا حسنا

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r7.claim: Shuayb says he does not intend to forbid something and then do it himself, answering their demand that he return to their religion.
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r7.anchor: يعني وما أريد أن أنهاكم عن أمر،

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r8.claim: Shuayb wants only as much reform as he can accomplish, and his success in doing good comes only from God.
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r8.anchor: يعني ما أريد { إلا الإصلاح ما استطعت وما توفيقي } في الإصلاح

MUQATIL:11:86-88/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:86-88/r9.claim: Shuayb trusts in God despite the threat to expel him and the believers, and says that the return after death is to God.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r1.claim: Good provision means prophethood and messengership or lawful wealth gained without cheating.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r1.anchor: ﴿ رزقا حسنا ﴾ يعنى النبوة والرسالة أو مالا حلالا من غير بخس وتطفيف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r2.claim: The answer to “Have you considered?” is omitted: should a truly commissioned prophet fail to command abandoning idols and sins?
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r2.anchor: وجواب أرأيتم محذوف أى أخبرونى إن كنت على حجة واضحة من ربى وكنت نبيا على الحقيقة أيصح لى أن لا آمركم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r3.claim: Khālafanī ilā means going toward something while the other turns away; khālafanī ʿanhu reverses those directions, illustrated by travelers at water.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r3.anchor: يقال خالفنى فلان إلى كذا إذا قصده و أنت مول عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r4.claim: Shuaib denies wanting to get ahead of them in indulging the desires he forbids, keeping them for himself.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r4.anchor: يعنى أن أسبقكم إلى شهواتكم التى نهيتكم عنها لاستبد بها دونكم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r5.claim: His only aim is reform through admonition, counsel, commanding right, and forbidding wrong.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r5.anchor: ما أريد إلا أن أصلحكم بموعظتى ونصيحتى وامرى بالمعروف ونهى عن المنكر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r6.claim: This is an adverbial expression meaning as long as he can work for reform and exert himself.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r6.anchor: ظرف أى مدة استطاعتى للاصلاح ومادمت متمكنا منه آلو فيه جهدا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r7.claim: Being enabled to reach the truth in action and restraint comes only through God's help and support.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r7.anchor: وما كونى موفقا لإصابة الحق فيما آنى وأذر إلا بمعونته وتأييده

NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r8.claim: He relies on God and returns to Him in prosperity and adversity.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p168/r8.anchor: ﴿ عليه توكلت ﴾ اعتمدت ﴿ وإليه أنيب ﴾ أرجع فى السراء والضراء

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r3.claim: Good provision means abundant, lawful wealth; Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Shuʿayb possessed great wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r3.anchor: أي واسعا حلالا، وكان شعيب عليه السلام كثير المال

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r4.claim: Alternatively, good provision means guidance, divine success, knowledge, and recognition.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد به الهدى والتوفيق، والعلم والمعرفة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r5.claim: The implied point is that Shuʿayb should forbid them from error.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r5.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف، وهو ما ذكرناه، أي أفلا أنهاكم عن الضلال

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r6.claim: Alternative rhetorical readings ask whether Shuʿayb should follow error with proof from God, or whether they may order him to cheat despite God's having enriched him.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى «أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي» أتبع الضلال؟

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r7.claim: The clause أن أخالفكم is in the accusative as the object of urīdu.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r8.claim: Shuʿayb does not forbid them something and then do it himself, just as he does not abandon what he commands them to do.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r8.anchor: أي ليس أنهاكم عن شيء وأرتكبه، كما لا أترك ما أمرتكم به

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r9.claim: He seeks reform as far as he can: justice improves their worldly life and worship their afterlife; capacity conditions action, while ما is a verbal noun meaning effort and ability.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r9.anchor: أي ما أريد إلا فعل الصلاح أي أن تصلحوا دنياكم بالعدل، وآخرتكم بالعبادة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r10.claim: Tawfīq means guidance or right direction.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r11.claim: To rely on God means to depend on Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r12.claim: Ināba means returning to God in all calamities; alternatives are returning to Him in the afterlife or supplicating to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:88-89/r12.anchor: أي أرجع فيما ينزل بي من جميع النوائب

RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r1.claim: The clear proof may mean the knowledge, guidance, religion, and prophethood God gave Shuʿayb; his good provision means the lawful wealth he received, as he was reportedly rich.
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله تعالى من العلم والهداية والدين والنبوة وقوله : { ورزقنى منه رزقا حسنا } إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله من المال الحلال

RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r2.claim: With the conditional answer omitted, Shuʿayb argues that having every spiritual and bodily blessing makes betrayal of God’s revelation and command unthinkable, answering their charge of inconsistency.
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r2.anchor: جواب إن الشرطية محذوف والتقدير : أنه تعالى لما آتاني جميع السعادات الروحانية وهي البينة والسعادات الجسمانية وهي المال والرزق الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the proof as certainty that idolatry and fraud are wrong; since Shuʿayb seeks their reform and needs none of their wealth, he cannot betray God’s revelation or judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r3.anchor: لما ثبت عندي أن الاشتغال بعبادة غير الله والاشتغال بالبخس والتطفيف عمل منكر

RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r4.claim: A third reading makes the proof a miracle and the good provision evidence that Shuʿayb asks no wage, like other prophets who say they seek reward only from the Lord of the worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r4.anchor: قوله : { إن كنت على بينة من ربى } أي ما حصل عنده من المعجزة

RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r5.claim: The phrase says provision came from God’s gift and aid, not from human earning; honor and abasement are God’s, so Shuʿayb is neither dismayed by opposition nor pleased by agreement, but clarifies God’s religion and law.
RAZI-FULL:v18p37/r5.anchor: يدل على أن ذلك الرزق إنما حصل من عند الله تعالى وبإعانته وأنه لا مدخل للكسب فيه

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf distinguishes ‘I differ from you toward it’ (I approach while you turn away) from ‘I differ from you away from it’; the verse means Shuʿayb will not seize their forbidden desires for himself.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : يقال خالفني فلان إلى كذا إذا قصده وأنت مول عنه وخالفني عنه إذا ولى عنه وأنت قاصده

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r2.claim: Since they concede his wisdom, Shuʿayb argues that sound reason chooses the best path: monotheism honors God and abandoning fraud shows compassion for His creatures, making this the noblest religion.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r2.anchor: الدعوة إلى توحيد الله تعالى وترك البخس والنقصان يرجع حاصلهما إلى جزأين ، التعظيم لأمر الله تعالى والشفقة على خلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r3.claim: Shuʿayb wants only to reform his people through counsel and admonition.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r3.anchor: والمعنى ما أريد إلا أن أصلحكم بموعظتي ونصيحتي

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r4.claim: ما استطعت may be a temporal phrase: for as long as Shuʿayb can work toward reform, he spares no effort.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r4.anchor: أنه ظرف والتقدير : مدة استطاعتي للإصلاح وما دمت متمكنا منه لا آلو فيه جهدا

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r5.claim: Alternatively, ما استطعت is an appositional specification of the amount of reform he can accomplish.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r5.anchor: أنه بدل من الإصلاح ، أي المقدار الذي استطعت منه

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r6.claim: A third parsing makes it the object of purpose: he seeks to reform whatever he is able to reform.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r6.anchor: أن يكون مفعولا له أي ما أريد إلا أن أصلح ما استطعت إصلاحه

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r7.claim: Their own recognition of his wisdom and reputation as a peacemaker supports his sincerity: he seeks reconciliation, not discord; his role is to convey and warn, not compel obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r7.anchor: وأما الإجبار على الطاعة فلا أقدر عليه ، ثم إنه عليه السلام أكد ذلك بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r8.claim: He relies on God’s guidance and enabling for the execution of every good act.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38/r8.anchor: وبين بهذا أن توكله واعتماده في تنفيذ كل الأعمال الصالحة على توفيق الله تعالى وهدايته

RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r1.claim: Tawakkul expresses pure monotheism and exclusive reliance: everything besides God is contingent and exists only through His bringing it into being; this is a highest level of knowledge of the Origin.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r1.anchor: لأن قوله عليه السلام توكلت يفيد

RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r2.claim: Turning back to God expresses exclusive return to Him and knowledge of the Hereafter.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r2.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى معرفة المعاد ، وهو أيضا يفيد الحصر لأن قوله : { وإليه أنيب } يدل على أنه لا مرجع للخلق إلا إلى الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r3.claim: The Prophet called Shuʿayb ‘the orator of the prophets,’ for his eloquent replies to his people; al-Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v18p38#2/r3.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا ذكر شعيب عليه السلام قال : ( ذاك خطيب الأنبياء )
